Options structure placeholder for image open operations. Currently only contains a dummy field; future versions may define fields. Passed to tsk_img_open*_opt functions.

struct TSK_VS_INFO {

        TSK_VS_TYPE_ENUM vstype;        ///< Type of volume system / media management

        TSK_DADDR_T offset;     ///< Byte offset where VS starts in disk image
        unsigned int block_size;        ///< Size of blocks in bytes

        TSK_ENDIAN_ENUM endian; ///< Endian ordering of data

        TSK_VS_PART_INFO *part_list;    ///< Linked list of partitions

        TSK_PNUM_T part_count;  ///< number of partitions

        void (*close) (TSK_VS_INFO *);  ///< \internal Progs should call tsk_vs_close().
    };
objects.description: Opaque/public C structure holding state for an open volume system (partitioning) within an image, including type, offsets, block size, endianness, partition list, and a close hook. The tag should equal TSK_VS_INFO_TAG while valid.

C struct representing a single partition/volume entry in a volume system. Forms a doubly-linked list via prev/next, references its parent TSK_VS_INFO, and records start, length, description, source table/slot, address, and flags. Validity can be checked with TSK_VS_PART_INFO_TAG.

objects.definition: typedef struct TSK_FS_FILE TSK_FS_FILE;
objects.description: Opaque forward declaration of a filesystem file handle/object used by TSK. Only a forward declaration is present here; the full definition is elsewhere.

Holds APFS filesystem-level metadata for fsstat-style reporting, including volume identifiers, capacity metrics, timestamps, unmount logs, and role/flags. Filled by tsk_apfs_fsstat. The struct layout implies fixed-size strings and arrays; APFS-specific types apfs_block_num and APFS_VOLUME_ROLE are defined in tsk_apfs.h.
Per-file APFS metadata used for istat-style reporting, including date added (timestamp), the inode number this file was cloned from (if any), and BSD file flags. Populated by tsk_apfs_istat.

Represents a single APFS snapshot entry: transaction ID (XID), creation timestamp, snapshot name (heap-allocated string), and a flag indicating a dataless snapshot. Instances are provided within an apfs_snapshot_list created by tsk_apfs_list_snapshots.

A variable-length array container of apfs_snapshot records. The flexible trailing array snapshots[0] holds num_snapshots elements. Memory is allocated and owned by the API; use tsk_apfs_free_snapshot_list to free. Created by tsk_apfs_list_snapshots.

Represents a journaled APFS object assembled from APFSJObjBtreeNode entries. Aggregates inode fields, directory children, data extents, inline and non-resident xattrs, name, sizes, and clone status. Provides lightweight validity checks and const accessors. Construction occurs from iterator ranges over the journal object B-tree.

Encapsulates access to APFS journal object tree(s). Holds crypto context, object and journal B-tree roots, and the root tree OID. Provides lookup of APFSJObject by OID, snapshot selection, and iteration via a nested forward iterator.
direct_api_constructors: APFSJObjTree(const APFSPool &pool, apfs_block_num obj_omap, uint64_t root_tree_oid, const APFSFileSystem::crypto_info_t &crypto)

objects.description: Forward iterator over APFSJObject entries produced by an APFSJObjTree. Stores a pointer to the owning tree, the next underlying B-tree iterator position, and the current materialized APFSJObject. Supports pre/post increment and standard iterator traits.

On-disk header for the com.apple.decmpfs extended attribute used by HFS+/APFS to store compression metadata (and possibly in-line compressed data). Fields are stored little-endian. attr_bytes is a flexible array member containing the attribute payload (either compressed bytes or additional data).

Enumeration of decmpfs compression/storage types indicating where and how compressed data is stored: in the attribute vs resource fork, algorithm (zlib or LZVN), raw/uncompressed, or dataless placeholder.

No custom data types (structs, enums, typedefs, or classes) are defined in this header. The file declares C functions related to filesystem encryption handling, but all referenced types (e.g., TSK_FS_INFO, TSK_DADDR_T) are declared elsewhere.
Common on-disk header present at the start of many APFS objects. Includes checksum, object ID, transaction ID, type, flags, and subtype.

        TSK_HDB_HTYPE_ENUM hash_type; ///< Type of hash used in currently open index
        uint16_t hash_len;            ///< Length of hash used in currently open index
        TSK_TCHAR *idx_fname;         ///< Name of index file, may be NULL for database without external index
        FILE *hIdx;                   ///< File handle to index (only open during lookups)
        FILE *hIdxTmp;                ///< File handle to temp (unsorted) index file (only open during index creation)
        TSK_TCHAR *uns_fname;         ///< Name of unsorted index file
        TSK_OFF_T idx_size;           ///< Size of index file
        uint16_t idx_off;             ///< Offset in index file to first index entry
        size_t idx_llen;              ///< Length of each line in index
        char *idx_lbuf;               ///< Buffer to hold a line from the index  (r/w shared - lock)
        TSK_TCHAR *idx_idx_fname;     ///< Name of index of index file, may be NULL
        uint64_t *idx_offsets;        ///< Maps the first three bytes of a hash value to an offset in the index file
    } TSK_HDB_BINSRCH_INFO;
objects.description: Concrete struct for text-format hash databases that use a TSK binary-searchable external index, embedding TSK_HDB_INFO plus file handles and index metadata/buffers.
Bit flags used when opening a hash database to control behavior (e.g., open only the index).
Callback function pointer type invoked during hash lookups; returns a TSK_WALK_RET_ENUM status. Note: TSK_WALK_RET_ENUM is declared elsewhere.
C++ RAII-style wrapper around TSK_HDB_INFO providing member methods to open databases, perform lookups, manage indexes, and query type. Destructor closes the underlying database.
Cache entry for an open logical file handle in a logical image. Stores the OS handle/FD, the file's inode number, and the last seek position for reusing the handle efficiently.
Cache entry mapping an inode number to its path and an age counter. Used to speed up lookups of logical file paths by inum.

objects.definition: struct LegacyCache;
objects.description: Forward declaration of an internal cache structure used by logical images. The actual definition is not present in this header, so its layout and lifetime rules are unknown.

Logical image IMG_INFO implementation. Extends IMG_INFO with base path, Windows object flag, an internal LegacyCache pointer, and several caches: per-block inum tracking, open file handle cache, and inum-to-path cache.

Container struct for a pool-backed image in The Sleuth Kit. It embeds a base IMG_INFO, references pool metadata (TSK_POOL_INFO), stores the starting block within the pool (pvol_block), and holds an implementation-specific pointer (impl). Full behavior and lifecycle are not documented here; infer that it is used to represent an image whose sectors are sourced from a pool volume.

objects.definition: typedef struct TSK_FS_ATTR_RUN TSK_FS_ATTR_RUN;
objects.description: Opaque forward declaration of a file-system attribute run structure. Only a pointer is exposed here; the actual definition is not in this header.
Enumeration of pool container types supported by the API, including autodetect, APFS, LVM, and an unsupported sentinel.
Bitmask flags describing per-volume properties within a pool (e.g., encrypted, case-sensitive).

objects.definition: typedef struct TSK_VS_PART_INFO TSK_VS_PART_INFO;
objects.description: Opaque forward declaration for a volume system partition info structure. The definition is not provided here.

objects.definition: typedef struct TSK_IMG_INFO TSK_IMG_INFO;
objects.description: Opaque forward declaration for image-info objects exposed by the TSK image layer. The definition is not provided here.

Node in a doubly linked list describing a single volume within a storage pool, including index, description, optional password hint, start block, length in blocks, and flags. Uses a tag for allocation validation and links to neighboring volumes.

objects.definition:
typedef struct _TSK_POOL_INFO {
  uint32_t tag;              ///< Set to TSK_POOL_INFO_TAG when struct is alloc
  TSK_POOL_TYPE_ENUM ctype;  ///< Type of pool container
  uint32_t block_size;       ///< Block size
  uint64_t num_blocks;       ///< Number of blocks
  int num_vols;              ///< Number of volumes
  uint64_t img_offset;       ///< The image offset of the pool
  TSK_POOL_VOLUME_INFO *vol_list;  ///< Linked list of volume info structs

  // Callbacks
  void (*close)(const struct _TSK_POOL_INFO *);  ///< \internal
  uint8_t (*poolstat)(const struct _TSK_POOL_INFO *pool,
                      FILE *hFile);  ///< \internal
  TSK_IMG_INFO* (*get_img_info)(const struct _TSK_POOL_INFO *pool,
      TSK_DADDR_T pvol_block);  ///< \internal

  void *impl;  ///< \internal Implementation specific pointer

} TSK_POOL_INFO;
objects.description: Top-level pool object describing a container of pooled volumes. Holds container type, geometry, image offset, linked-list head of TSK_POOL_VOLUME_INFO, and internal callback function pointers plus an implementation-specific pointer. Must be obtained via tsk_pool_open* APIs and released with tsk_pool_close.

Abstract base class representing a pool of one or more disk images with block-based addressing. Manages member images (TSK_IMG_INFO pointers with offsets), pool UUID, block sizes, counts, and volume count. Not default-constructible or copyable; moveable. Subclasses must implement read() and may override unallocated_ranges().

objects.definition: using img_t = std::pair<TSK_IMG_INFO *const, const TSK_OFF_T>;
objects.description: Alias type within TSKPool representing a single pool member: a pair of a TSK_IMG_INFO pointer (const-qualified pointer object) and a const TSK_OFF_T offset for the first byte/block of that image within the pool.
Alias to an unnamed struct describing a block range: starting block index and number of blocks. Used to report unallocated ranges in the pool.

objects.definition: typedef uint64_t apfs_block_num;
objects.description: Alias for a 64-bit unsigned integer representing an APFS block number within an APFS pool or container. Used to identify specific blocks; special constants in this header define sentinel values for selection of versions (e.g., last known good or latest). Destruction/ownership are not applicable since it is a typedef to a fundamental type.

Opaque APFS block wrapper that owns a fixed-size storage buffer for one APFS block, knows its pool and block number, and provides decrypt, dump, and comparison utilities. Non-copyable, move-constructible. Constructed with a pool and block number; intended to be retrieved and cached by APFSPool.

APFS pool abstraction built on TSKPool. Manages APFS container images, block cache, reading, known versions, and volume discovery. Non-copyable; move-enabled. Provides block caching via get_block, and exposes hardware_crypto, nx superblock access, and unallocated ranges.

C++ compatibility wrapper class for an APFS pool, derived from TSKPoolCompat specialized with APFSPool. It initializes APFS volumes on construction, provides a destructor, and exposes poolstat and getImageInfo helper methods compatible with The Sleuth Kit APIs. Details about ownership and resource management are not documented here; infer that it manages/coordinates access to an APFS pool within TSK.

A value-type wrapper representing a 16-byte GUID/UUID. Instances can be constructed from raw bytes, C-style byte arrays, strings, or default-constructed (empty). Provides string conversion, byte access, copy/move semantics, and equality/inequality. Actual storage is a std::vector<unsigned char> holding the 16 bytes.

Factory class for producing new TSKGuid instances. On non-Android platforms it has a trivial default constructor; on Android it stores JNI context needed to call into Java to generate UUIDs. The newGuid() method returns a freshly generated TSKGuid.
Enumeration controlling traversal flow in the automated extraction framework: continue, stop entirely, or skip current object.

Primary C++ automation class that orchestrates image, volume, pool, and filesystem traversal and invokes user overrides (processFile, filters). Manages error recording, optional image writer, and recursion control. Users subclass and implement processFile (and optionally processAttribute, filter*). Construction via default ctor; destruction via virtual dtor. Owns internal state but may reference external TSK_* structures not owned here.
Nested POD used by TskAuto to record an error code and up to two message strings for later retrieval/logging.

Concrete helper class deriving from TskAuto that scans an input image and records whether data, filesystems, or encryption artifacts are present, determining if the image is supported by Sleuth Kit. Public methods expose the result, error messages, and printing utilities. Construction is default; lifecycle and traversal logic are handled via TskAuto callbacks (processFile, filterVol/Pool/PoolVol/Fs, handleError).
Enumeration indicating how (or whether) encryption was detected. Values: NONE (no encryption detected), SIGNATURE (detected via known on-disk signatures), ENTROPY (detected via statistical entropy).

Result object returned by encryption detection functions. Contains the detection type and a human-readable description string. Memory ownership/creation details are not specified in this header; callers should consult implementation or project conventions for allocation and freeing.

Type is referenced but not defined in this header. It is likely a platform-dependent character type (e.g., wchar_t or char) used across The Sleuth Kit, but there is no definition here to include. Cannot document further without its defining header.

Type is referenced but not defined in this header. It likely represents a file-offset or size integral type used by The Sleuth Kit, but there is no definition here to include. Cannot document further without its defining header.

objects.definition: struct in_place_t {};
objects.description: Tag type used to request in-place construction of an object managed by lw_shared_ptr. Instances of this tag signal that the pointee should be constructed directly within the shared allocation.

A specialization-like convenience struct for viewing raw memory as bytes. Inherits span<char> and reuses its constructors. Provides template as<T>() to reinterpret the underlying storage pointer as a T*. Does not perform size or alignment checks; caller must ensure correctness and lifetime of underlying memory.

Packed-on-disk representation of a BSD disk label used by The Sleuth Kit. All fields are byte arrays (big/little-endian handling occurs elsewhere). Includes overall geometry/metadata (magic, type, sizes), and an array of 16 partition entries (part), each with size, start, fragment sizing, filesystem type, and cylinders-per-group. Struct size is 512 bytes. The inner partition struct is an anonymous, inline definition and not a separately named type.

Represents a DOS/MBR partition table entry. Fields include boot indicator, start/end CHS addresses, partition type, starting LBA (little-endian 4 bytes), and size in sectors (little-endian 4 bytes). Used to parse the four 16-byte entries in a traditional MBR.

Represents a DOS/MBR boot sector containing the partition table. Includes initial jump/loader bytes (f1), OEM name, sector size, cluster size, filler to align to partition table, an array of four partition entries (ptable), and the boot sector signature (magic), expected to be 0x55 0xAA. Used for identifying and parsing MBR structures.

GUID structure used by GPT to represent partition types and unique identifiers. Matches the standard GUID layout (32-bit, 16-bit, 16-bit, and 8-byte array). Endianness and on-disk byte order considerations apply when parsing from disk sectors.

Raw on-disk GPT header structure as laid out in sector 1. All fields are byte arrays as stored on disk and require decoding (endianness, width) before use. Contains disk GUID and locations/sizes of the partition entry array and backup header.

Raw GPT partition entry as stored in the partition entry array. Includes type GUID, unique partition GUID, start/end LBAs, attribute flags, and UTF-16LE name (72 bytes). Values must be parsed from little-endian byte arrays.
Enumeration indicating whether a GPT structure refers to the primary (at the beginning of the disk) or secondary (backup at the end of the disk) table.

Structure representing a classic Apple Partition Map (APM) entry as used by The Sleuth Kit. All fields are stored as raw big-endian byte arrays matching on-disk layout. Key fields include magic (signature), partition map size, partition start and size in sectors, human-readable name and type, data region start/size, status flags, and boot-related parameters (start, size, load address, entry point, checksum) plus processor type. Reserved arrays preserve alignment and on-disk padding. Callers are responsible for endianness conversion and interpreting flags. No constructors or owners are defined in this header.

On-disk Sun SPARC disk label (VTOC) structure as laid out in bytes. All fields are stored as raw byte arrays in big-endian on media; consumers must decode endianness/packing. Contains ASCII label, VTOC metadata, per-partition metadata and layout (start cylinder and block count), and trailer magic/checksum. Intended for parsing Sun/SPARC disk labels within The Sleuth Kit. Ownership and lifetime are plain C value semantics; no dynamic members.

On-disk Sun i386 disk label (VTOC) structure as raw bytes. Fields are stored as byte arrays; callers must interpret endianness (typically little-endian for i386 on media), sizes, and packing. Includes VTOC header, up to 16 partition entries with start sector and size, timestamps, and drive geometry fields with magic/checksum trailer. Value type with no dynamic allocation.

functions.name: tsk_error_get_info
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the per-thread error information structure used by the TSK library. Callers can read and (indirectly via helpers) modify error code and messages for the current thread.
requirements: Must be called from a context where TSK per-thread state has been initialized (library usage).
Return pointer is managed by the library; do not free it.
Pointer is thread-local; use only within the calling thread.

functions.name: tsk_error_get_errno
functions.description: Gets the current error number for the calling thread’s TSK error state.
requirements: Returns 0 or a TSK_ERR_* value depending on current error state.
Call is thread-local; it retrieves errno for the calling thread.

functions.name: tsk_error_set_errno
functions.description: Sets the current error number for the calling thread’s TSK error state.
requirements: t_errno should be a TSK_ERR_* value or 0 to clear, based on library conventions.
Affects only the calling thread’s error state.

functions.name: tsk_error_get_errstr
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the current primary error message string for the calling thread.
requirements: Returned pointer is owned by the library; do not free or modify beyond standard read usage.
String may be empty if no error is set.
Thread-local to the calling thread.

functions.name: tsk_error_set_errstr
functions.description: Formats and sets the primary error message string for the calling thread using printf-style formatting.
requirements: format must be a valid printf-style format string.
The variadic arguments must match the format specifiers.
Affects only the calling thread’s error state.

functions.name: tsk_error_vset_errstr
functions.description: va_list variant of tsk_error_set_errstr; sets the primary error message using a va_list.
requirements: format must be a valid printf-style format string.
args must be a valid, initialized va_list corresponding to format.
Affects only the calling thread’s error state.

functions.name: tsk_error_get_errstr2
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the secondary error message string for the calling thread.
requirements: Returned pointer is library-managed; do not free.
String may be empty if unset.
Thread-local to the calling thread.

functions.name: tsk_error_set_errstr2
functions.description: Formats and sets the secondary error message string for the calling thread using printf-style formatting.
requirements: format must be a valid printf-style format string.
Variadic arguments must match the format specifiers.
Affects only the calling thread’s error state.

functions.name: tsk_error_vset_errstr2
functions.description: va_list variant to set the secondary error message for the calling thread.
requirements: format must be a valid printf-style format string.
args must be a valid, initialized va_list corresponding to format.
Affects only the calling thread’s error state.

functions.name: tsk_error_errstr2_concat
functions.description: Appends formatted text to the secondary error message for the calling thread using printf-style formatting.
requirements: format must be a valid printf-style format string.
Variadic arguments must match the format specifiers.
Affects only the calling thread’s error state.

functions.name: tsk_error_set_error_listener
functions.description: Registers a callback invoked on error events; the callback receives errno and an error message string.
requirements: listener must be a function pointer compatible with: void (*)(unsigned int errno, const char* errmsg).
Listener will be called from within TSK error reporting; it must be reentrant/thread-safe as appropriate for the application.
Passing NULL likely clears the listener (exact behavior not documented).

functions.name: tsk_error_get
functions.description: Returns a human-readable string corresponding to the current error code for the calling thread.
requirements: Returned pointer is library-managed; do not free.
May return NULL if there is no error set (per comment).
Thread-local to the calling thread.

functions.name: tsk_error_print
functions.description: Prints the current error message to the given FILE stream.
requirements: FILE* must be a valid, open stream suitable for writing.
Prints the current thread’s error message.

functions.name: tsk_error_reset
functions.description: Clears the current error number and error messages for the calling thread.
requirements: Affects only the calling thread’s error state.

functions.name: tsk_list_find
functions.description: Searches a TSK_LIST for a given key within its runs; returns non-zero if found, zero otherwise. The list stores runs where key marks the largest value and len indicates length (stored as positive, representing a negative run length).
requirements: list must point to a valid TSK_LIST or be NULL if no list is present (exact NULL behavior not documented).
key is the value to search for.

functions.name: tsk_list_add
functions.description: Adds a key to the linked list of runs, potentially creating or extending a run; the list is maintained in reverse sort order for faster inserts.
requirements: list must be a valid pointer to a TSK_LIST* (address of the head pointer) so the function can update the head.
The function may allocate memory for new nodes; caller should later free the list with tsk_list_free.
key is the value to add.

functions.name: tsk_list_free
functions.description: Frees all nodes in a TSK_LIST linked list.
requirements: list must be either NULL or a pointer to a list previously managed by tsk_list_add or compatible allocation.
After return, the list memory is released; the caller should not use freed nodes.

functions.name: tsk_stack_push
functions.description: Pushes a value onto the TSK_STACK. Used for tracking recursion/loop detection.
requirements: stack must be a valid pointer to a TSK_STACK created by tsk_stack_create.
Returns 1 on error (per C++ wrapper doc); check return value before proceeding.
key is the value to push.

functions.name: tsk_stack_pop
functions.description: Pops the top value from the TSK_STACK.
requirements: stack must be a valid pointer to a TSK_STACK created by tsk_stack_create.
Behavior when popping an empty stack is not documented; callers should ensure non-empty before popping.

functions.name: tsk_stack_find
functions.description: Searches the TSK_STACK for a given value; returns 1 if found, 0 if not (per C++ wrapper doc).
requirements: stack must be a valid pointer to a TSK_STACK created by tsk_stack_create.
key is the value to search for.

functions.name: tsk_stack_free
functions.description: Frees the memory associated with a TSK_STACK.
requirements: stack must be either NULL or a pointer returned by tsk_stack_create.
After free, the pointer becomes invalid; do not use the stack unless recreated.

functions.name: tsk_stack_create
functions.description: Allocates and initializes a new TSK_STACK instance and returns its pointer.
requirements: Returns NULL on allocation failure; callers should check for NULL before use.
The returned stack must be freed with tsk_stack_free.

functions.name: tsk_fprintf
functions.description: Prints a UTF-8 internal string to a FILE stream converting to the local platform’s Unicode/encoding as needed; printf-style formatting supported.
requirements: fd must be a valid, open FILE* for writing.
msg must be a valid printf-style format string; arguments must match the format.

functions.name: tsk_printf
functions.description: Prints a UTF-8 internal string to standard output (or platform-appropriate console) converting to the local platform’s Unicode/encoding; printf-style formatting supported.
requirements: msg must be a valid printf-style format string; arguments must match the format.

functions.name: tsk_print_sanitized
functions.description: Prints a path or string to the given FILE stream while removing or escaping special characters.
requirements: fd must be a valid, open FILE* for writing.
str must be a valid, null-terminated string.

functions.name: tsk_version_print
functions.description: Prints the TSK library version string to the provided FILE stream.
requirements: FILE* must be a valid, open stream suitable for writing.

functions.name: tsk_version_get_str
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the TSK library version string (string form).
requirements: Returned pointer is library-managed; do not free or modify.

functions.name: tsk_parse_offset
functions.description: Parses a textual offset into a TSK_OFF_T value. Exact accepted formats depend on platform and library conventions.
requirements: Input must be a valid, null-terminated TSK_TCHAR string representing an offset.
Caller should validate the return value according to expected range; detailed error signaling is not specified.

functions.name: tsk_parse_pnum
functions.description: Parses a textual partition number into a TSK_PNUM_T output parameter.
requirements: a_pnum_str must be a valid, null-terminated TSK_TCHAR string representing a partition number.
a_pnum must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the parsed value.
Return value should be checked for success/failure (exact convention not documented).

functions.name: TSK_MD5_Init
functions.description: Initializes an MD5 context prior to hashing data.
requirements: Context pointer must be non-NULL and point to writable TSK_MD5_CTX storage.
Must be called before TSK_MD5_Update/TSK_MD5_Final on the same context.

functions.name: TSK_MD5_Update
functions.signature: void TSK_MD5_Update(TSK_MD5_CTX *, const unsigned char *, unsigned int);
functions.description: Updates an MD5 context with a buffer of data.
requirements: Context must have been initialized with TSK_MD5_Init.
Data pointer must be valid if count > 0; count is the number of bytes to process.

functions.name: TSK_MD5_Final
functions.description: Finalizes the MD5 computation and writes the 16-byte digest to the output buffer.
requirements: Context must have been initialized and updated as needed.
Output buffer must have space for exactly 16 bytes (TSK_MD5_DIGEST_LENGTH).

functions.name: TSK_SHA_Init
functions.description: Initializes a SHA context prior to hashing data (SHA-1 per structure layout; macro defines digest length).
requirements: Context pointer must be non-NULL and point to writable TSK_SHA_CTX storage.
Must be called before TSK_SHA_Update/TSK_SHA_Final on the same context.

functions.name: TSK_SHA_Update
functions.signature: void TSK_SHA_Update(TSK_SHA_CTX *, const BYTE *buffer, unsigned int count);
functions.description: Updates the SHA context with a buffer of data.
requirements: Context must have been initialized with TSK_SHA_Init.
buffer must be valid if count > 0; count is the number of bytes to process.

functions.name: TSK_SHA_Final
functions.description: Finalizes the SHA computation and writes the message digest to the output buffer. The required size is defined by TSK_SHA_DIGEST_LENGTH.
requirements: Context must have been initialized and updated as needed.
output must point to a buffer large enough for TSK_SHA_DIGEST_LENGTH bytes.

functions.name: TskError::get
functions.description: C++ convenience wrapper that returns the current error message string for the thread (calls tsk_error_get).
requirements: Returned pointer is library-managed; do not free.
Usable from C++ code that includes the class definition.

functions.name: TskError::print
functions.description: C++ convenience wrapper to print the current error message to the given FILE stream (calls tsk_error_print).
requirements: a_hFile must be a valid, open FILE* for writing.

functions.name: TskError::reset
functions.description: C++ convenience wrapper that clears the current error number and messages for the thread (calls tsk_error_reset).
requirements: Affects only the calling thread’s error state.

functions.name: tsk_img_open_sing
functions.signature: TSK_IMG_INFO *tsk_img_open_sing(const TSK_TCHAR * a_image, TSK_IMG_TYPE_ENUM type, unsigned int a_ssize);
functions.description: Opens a single (non-split) disk image for reading and returns an opaque TSK_IMG_INFO handle describing the image. The image type can be explicitly specified or autodetected; the sector size can be set or left as 0 to use a default. Use the returned handle with tsk_img_read() and close it with tsk_img_close().
requirements: a_image must point to a valid, accessible path to a single image file.
type may be TSK_IMG_TYPE_DETECT for autodetection, or a specific supported type.
a_ssize can be 0 (use default) or a valid device sector size in bytes.
Caller must eventually call tsk_img_close() on the returned TSK_IMG_INFO* to release resources.
On failure, returns NULL; caller must check for NULL before using the handle.

functions.name: tsk_img_open
functions.signature: TSK_IMG_INFO *tsk_img_open(int num_img, const TSK_TCHAR * const images[], TSK_IMG_TYPE_ENUM, unsigned int a_ssize);
functions.description: Opens one or more disk image files (e.g., split/raw sets) for reading and returns a TSK_IMG_INFO handle. The image type can be specified or autodetected; sector size may be specified or defaulted. Subsequent reads are done via tsk_img_read(); close with tsk_img_close().
requirements: num_img must equal the number of elements in images[].
images must contain exactly num_img paths and be in sorted order (per comment).
Each images[i] must be a valid, accessible path.
The image type parameter may be TSK_IMG_TYPE_DETECT or a specific supported type.
a_ssize can be 0 (use default) or a valid device sector size in bytes.
Returns NULL on failure; caller must check for NULL before use.
Caller must close the handle with tsk_img_close() when done.

functions.name: tsk_img_open_utf8_sing
functions.signature: TSK_IMG_INFO *tsk_img_open_utf8_sing(const char *a_image, TSK_IMG_TYPE_ENUM type, unsigned int a_ssize);
functions.description: UTF-8 path variant of tsk_img_open_sing(). Opens a single image file and returns a TSK_IMG_INFO handle. Intended especially for Windows builds that need UTF-8 paths.
requirements: a_image must be a UTF-8 encoded path to an accessible image file.
type may be TSK_IMG_TYPE_DETECT or a specific supported type.
a_ssize can be 0 (use default) or a valid device sector size.
Returns NULL on failure; caller must check.
Caller must close with tsk_img_close() when finished.

functions.name: tsk_img_open_utf8
functions.signature: TSK_IMG_INFO *tsk_img_open_utf8(int num_img, const char *const images[], TSK_IMG_TYPE_ENUM type, unsigned int a_ssize);
functions.description: UTF-8 path variant of tsk_img_open(). Opens one or more image files and returns a TSK_IMG_INFO handle.
requirements: num_img must equal the number of elements in images[].
images must contain exactly num_img UTF-8 encoded paths in sorted order.
Each images[i] must be an accessible file path.
type may be TSK_IMG_TYPE_DETECT or a specific supported type.
a_ssize can be 0 (use default) or a valid device sector size.
Returns NULL on failure; caller must check.
Caller must close with tsk_img_close() when done.

functions.name: tsk_img_open_sing_opt
functions.signature: TSK_IMG_INFO *tsk_img_open_sing_opt(const TSK_TCHAR * a_image, TSK_IMG_TYPE_ENUM type, unsigned int a_ssize, const TSK_IMG_OPTIONS* opts);
functions.description: Like tsk_img_open_sing() but accepts additional image options via opts. Returns a TSK_IMG_INFO handle on success.
requirements: a_image must be a valid path to a single image file.
type may be TSK_IMG_TYPE_DETECT or a specific supported type.
a_ssize can be 0 (use default) or a valid sector size.
opts may be NULL or a pointer to a TSK_IMG_OPTIONS structure (fields unspecified in this header).
Returns NULL on failure; caller must check and must close successful handles with tsk_img_close().

functions.name: tsk_img_open_opt
functions.signature: TSK_IMG_INFO *tsk_img_open_opt(int num_img, const TSK_TCHAR * const images[], TSK_IMG_TYPE_ENUM, unsigned int a_ssize, const TSK_IMG_OPTIONS* opts);
functions.description: Like tsk_img_open() but accepts additional image options via opts.
requirements: num_img must equal the number of elements in images[].
images must contain exactly num_img paths in sorted order.
Each images[i] must be an accessible file path.
The image type parameter may be TSK_IMG_TYPE_DETECT or a specific supported type.
a_ssize can be 0 (use default) or a valid sector size.
opts may be NULL or a pointer to a TSK_IMG_OPTIONS structure (fields unspecified here).
Returns NULL on failure; caller must check; successful handles must be closed with tsk_img_close().

functions.name: tsk_img_open_utf8_sing_opt
functions.signature: TSK_IMG_INFO *tsk_img_open_utf8_sing_opt(const char *a_image, TSK_IMG_TYPE_ENUM type, unsigned int a_ssize, const TSK_IMG_OPTIONS* opts);
functions.description: UTF-8 path variant of tsk_img_open_sing_opt(). Opens a single image with optional parameters.
requirements: a_image must be a UTF-8 encoded path to an accessible image file.
type may be TSK_IMG_TYPE_DETECT or a specific supported type.
a_ssize can be 0 (use default) or a valid sector size.
opts may be NULL or a pointer to TSK_IMG_OPTIONS.
Returns NULL on failure; caller must check; close with tsk_img_close() on success.

functions.name: tsk_img_open_utf8_opt
functions.signature: TSK_IMG_INFO* tsk_img_open_utf8_opt(int num_img, const char *const images[], TSK_IMG_TYPE_ENUM type, unsigned int a_ssize, const TSK_IMG_OPTIONS* opts);
functions.description: UTF-8 path variant of tsk_img_open_opt(). Opens one or more images with optional parameters.
requirements: num_img must equal the number of elements in images[].
images must contain exactly num_img UTF-8 encoded paths in sorted order.
Each images[i] must be an accessible file path.
type may be TSK_IMG_TYPE_DETECT or a specific supported type.
a_ssize can be 0 (use default) or a valid sector size.
opts may be NULL or a pointer to TSK_IMG_OPTIONS.
Returns NULL on failure; caller must check; close with tsk_img_close() on success.

functions.name: tsk_img_open_external
functions.signature: TSK_IMG_INFO *tsk_img_open_external(void* ext_img_info, TSK_OFF_T size, unsigned int sector_size, ssize_t(*read) (TSK_IMG_INFO * img, TSK_OFF_T off, char *buf, size_t len), void (*close) (TSK_IMG_INFO *), void (*imgstat) (TSK_IMG_INFO *, FILE *));
functions.description: Registers an externally-implemented image source with TSK by supplying callbacks for read, close, and imgstat along with size and sector size. Returns a TSK_IMG_INFO that wraps the external image.
requirements: ext_img_info may be an opaque pointer passed back to callbacks; semantics are implementation-defined.
size must be the total image size in bytes; should be non-negative and accurate.
sector_size should be the device sector size in bytes (typically 512); should be > 0.

read callback must be a valid function pointer with signature ssize_t(TSK_IMG_INFO*, TSK_OFF_T, char*, size_t) and obey standard semantics: fill buf with up to len bytes from off; return bytes read or -1 on error.
close callback must be a valid function pointer taking TSK_IMG_INFO* and releasing resources created by the external implementation.
imgstat callback must be a valid function pointer for printing image stats to FILE*; may be NULL if not supported (unknown; header does not specify, so treat non-NULL as safest).
All callback pointers must remain valid for the lifetime of the returned TSK_IMG_INFO.
Returns NULL on failure; caller must check and close the handle (via provided close callback through tsk_img_close()) on success.

functions.name: tsk_img_close
functions.description: Closes a TSK_IMG_INFO previously returned by an open function and releases associated resources. For external images, invokes the registered close callback.
requirements: The argument must be a TSK_IMG_INFO* returned by a successful open function or NULL (behavior on NULL is unknown; safest to pass only valid handles).
After calling, the handle must not be used again.

functions.name: tsk_img_read
functions.signature: ssize_t tsk_img_read(TSK_IMG_INFO * img, TSK_OFF_T off, char *buf, size_t len);
functions.description: Reads up to len bytes from the image starting at byte offset off into buf. Returns the number of bytes read or -1 on error.
requirements: img must be a valid, open TSK_IMG_INFO*.
buf must point to a writable buffer of at least len bytes.
off should be within [0, image_size); behavior for offsets beyond end is implementation-defined; expect fewer bytes or error.
len may be any non-negative size_t; short reads may occur at end-of-image.
Caller must check for -1 to detect errors and handle partial reads.

functions.name: tsk_img_type_toid_utf8
functions.description: Parses a UTF-8 string specifying an image format and returns the corresponding TSK_IMG_TYPE_ENUM value. Used to parse command-line or user input.
requirements: Input string must be a valid, null-terminated UTF-8 C string.
Returns a TSK_IMG_TYPE_ENUM; mapping specifics depend on implementation (unknown).
Caller should handle unrecognized strings mapping to TSK_IMG_TYPE_UNSUPP or similar (exact behavior unknown).

functions.name: tsk_img_type_toid
functions.description: Parses a TSK_TCHAR string specifying an image format and returns the corresponding TSK_IMG_TYPE_ENUM value.
requirements: Input must be a valid, null-terminated TSK_TCHAR string.
Caller should handle unrecognized strings mapping to an unsupported/unknown enum (exact mapping unknown).

functions.name: tsk_img_type_toname
functions.description: Returns the short name string for an image format enum value.
requirements: Argument must be a valid TSK_IMG_TYPE_ENUM value.
Return is a pointer to a static or internal string; caller must not free it.
For unsupported values, may return a placeholder or NULL (behavior unknown); caller should check.

functions.name: tsk_img_type_todesc
functions.description: Returns a human-readable description string for an image format enum value.
requirements: Argument must be a valid TSK_IMG_TYPE_ENUM value.
Return is a pointer to a static or internal string; caller must not free it.
For unsupported values, may return a placeholder or NULL (behavior unknown); caller should check.

functions.name: tsk_img_type_supported
functions.description: Returns a bitmask of supported image format types. Each bit corresponds to a TSK_IMG_TYPE_ENUM value that is supported by the current build.
requirements: No arguments.
Caller should interpret the return as a bitmask; use TSK_IMG_TYPE_ISXXX macros to test categories.

functions.name: tsk_img_type_print
functions.description: Prints the name and description of supported image types to the given FILE stream (e.g., stdout/stderr).
requirements: FILE* must be a valid stream opened for writing.
Caller manages the FILE* lifetime; function does not close it.

functions.name: TskImgInfo::open
functions.signature: uint8_t TskImgInfo::open(const TSK_TCHAR * a_image, TSK_IMG_TYPE_ENUM a_type, unsigned int a_ssize);
functions.description: C++ wrapper method to open a single (non-split) image using tsk_img_open_sing(). Returns 0 on success, 1 on error. On success, stores the internal TSK_IMG_INFO and marks the object as opened.
requirements: a_image must be a valid path string.
a_type may be autodetect or a specific type.
a_ssize can be 0 or a sector size in bytes.
Must not be called on an object that already manages an open image without first destroying or closing (the class destructor calls tsk_img_close(); explicit close method is not provided).
Caller must check the return value: 0 means success, 1 means failure.

functions.name: TskImgInfo::open
functions.signature: uint8_t TskImgInfo::open(int a_num_img, const TSK_TCHAR * const a_images[], TSK_IMG_TYPE_ENUM a_type, unsigned int a_ssize);
functions.description: C++ wrapper to open multiple image files using tsk_img_open(). Returns 0 on success, 1 on error.
requirements: a_num_img must equal the number of elements in a_images[].
a_images must contain exactly a_num_img paths in sorted order.
a_type may be autodetect or a specific type.
a_ssize can be 0 or a sector size in bytes.
Do not call on an instance that already wraps an open image without allowing destructor to close it.
Caller must check return value (0 success, 1 error).

functions.name: TskImgInfo::read
functions.signature: ssize_t TskImgInfo::read(TSK_OFF_T a_off, char *a_buf, size_t a_len);
functions.description: C++ convenience wrapper for tsk_img_read(). Reads up to a_len bytes at offset a_off into a_buf. Returns number of bytes read or -1 on error.
requirements: This instance must currently wrap a valid TSK_IMG_INFO (i.e., open() previously succeeded).
a_buf must be a writable buffer of at least a_len bytes.
a_off should be within the image bounds; partial reads may occur at EOF.
Caller must handle -1 return and partial reads.

functions.name: TskImgInfo::getType
functions.description: Returns the image format type of the wrapped image, or 0 if no image is open.
requirements: Safe to call at any time; returns 0 cast to TSK_IMG_TYPE_ENUM if no image is open.
No ownership transfer.

functions.name: TskImgInfo::getSize
functions.description: Returns the total size in bytes of the wrapped image, or 0 if no image is open.
requirements: Safe to call if no image is open (returns 0).

functions.name: TskImgInfo::getSectorSize
functions.description: Returns the device sector size in bytes of the wrapped image, or 0 if no image is open.
requirements: Safe to call if no image is open (returns 0).

functions.name: TskImgInfo::typeToId
functions.description: Static convenience wrapper around tsk_img_type_toid(). Converts a format string to a TSK_IMG_TYPE_ENUM.
requirements: a_str must be a valid TSK_TCHAR string.
Return value must be interpreted by caller; unsupported strings mapping behavior is implementation-defined (unknown).

functions.name: TskImgInfo::typeToName
functions.description: Static convenience wrapper around tsk_img_type_toname(). Returns a short name for a_type.
requirements: a_type should be a valid TSK_IMG_TYPE_ENUM.
Returned pointer must not be freed.

functions.name: TskImgInfo::typeToDesc
functions.description: Static convenience wrapper around tsk_img_type_todesc(). Returns a human-readable description for a_type.
requirements: a_type should be a valid TSK_IMG_TYPE_ENUM.
Returned pointer must not be freed.

functions.name: TskImgInfo::typeSupported
functions.description: Static convenience wrapper around tsk_img_type_supported(). Returns a bitmask of supported image types.
requirements: No arguments. Caller should treat return value as a bitmask.

functions.name: TskImgInfo::typePrint
functions.description: Static convenience wrapper around tsk_img_type_print(). Prints supported image types to the given stream.
requirements: a_file must be a valid FILE* open for writing.

functions.name: tsk_vs_type_toid
functions.description: Parses a volume system type string into its internal TSK_VS_TYPE_ENUM identifier. Intended to convert user input to an enum for opening/processing volume systems.
requirements: Input string must be a valid, null-terminated TSK_TCHAR string.
Returns an enum value; unsupported/unknown names map to an unsupported identifier per library behavior (exact mapping details unknown).

functions.name: tsk_vs_type_toid_utf8
functions.description: Parses a UTF-8 volume system type string into its internal TSK_VS_TYPE_ENUM identifier. UTF-8 variant of tsk_vs_type_toid.
requirements: Input must be a valid, null-terminated UTF-8 C string.
Returns an enum value; unknown names map to an unsupported identifier (exact mapping details unknown).

functions.name: tsk_vs_type_toname
functions.description: Returns the short string name for a given volume system type identifier.
requirements: Argument must be a valid TSK_VS_TYPE_ENUM value.
Returns a pointer to a constant string or NULL on error/unknown (exact error conditions unknown).
Caller must not modify or free the returned string.

functions.name: tsk_vs_type_todesc
functions.description: Returns a human-readable description string for a given volume system type identifier.
requirements: Argument must be a valid TSK_VS_TYPE_ENUM value.
Returns a pointer to a constant string or NULL on error/unknown (exact error conditions unknown).
Caller must not modify or free the returned string.

functions.name: tsk_vs_type_supported
functions.description: Returns a bitmask of supported volume system types. Each supported type has its bit set in the return value.
requirements: No arguments.
Interpret the return as a bitmask over TSK_VS_TYPE_ENUM values (exact bit layout per enum constants).

functions.name: tsk_vs_type_print
functions.description: Prints the supported volume system type names to the given FILE stream.
requirements: FILE* must be a valid, open stream for writing.
No return value; caller must handle I/O errors via the stream (if any).

functions.name: tsk_vs_open
functions.description: Opens and analyzes the volume system at the given byte offset in an image, returning a handle for subsequent VS operations.
requirements: TSK_IMG_INFO* must reference a valid, already-open disk image.
Offset argument is a byte offset from the start of the image.
Type may be a specific TSK_VS_TYPE_ENUM or TSK_VS_TYPE_DETECT for auto-detection.
Returns a non-NULL TSK_VS_INFO* on success, or NULL on error. Caller must close with tsk_vs_close().

functions.name: tsk_vs_close
functions.description: Closes and frees resources associated with an open volume system handle created by tsk_vs_open.
requirements: Argument must be a TSK_VS_INFO* previously returned by tsk_vs_open.
Do not use the handle after calling this function.
Safe behavior if passed NULL is unknown.

functions.name: tsk_vs_read_block
functions.signature: ssize_t tsk_vs_read_block(TSK_VS_INFO * a_vs, TSK_DADDR_T a_addr, char *buf, size_t len);
functions.description: Reads one or more blocks from the volume system at a block address relative to the start of the volume system into the buffer.
requirements: a_vs must be a valid open TSK_VS_INFO*.
a_addr is a sector/block address relative to the start of the volume system.
buf must point to a writable buffer of at least len bytes.
len is in bytes and must be a multiple of the volume system block_size (per class documentation referencing this function).
Returns number of bytes read or -1 on error.

functions.name: tsk_vs_part_get
functions.description: Returns a pointer to partition metadata for the partition at the given 0-based index within the volume system.
requirements: VS handle must be valid and open.
idx is a 0-based partition index within [0, part_count).
Returns a pointer to an internal const TSK_VS_PART_INFO or NULL on error/out of range. Caller must not free or modify the returned struct.

functions.name: tsk_vs_part_walk
functions.signature: uint8_t tsk_vs_part_walk(TSK_VS_INFO * vs, TSK_PNUM_T start, TSK_PNUM_T last, TSK_VS_PART_FLAG_ENUM flags, TSK_VS_PART_WALK_CB action, void *ptr);
functions.description: Iterates over partitions in the given index range and invokes the callback for each partition matching the flags filter.
requirements: vs must be a valid open TSK_VS_INFO*.
start and last define the 0-based inclusive index range to walk; they should be within [0, part_count) and start <= last (exact bounds behavior unknown).
flags selects which partitions to visit (e.g., ALLOC/UNALLOC/META/ALL).
action must be a valid callback function pointer conforming to TSK_VS_PART_WALK_CB.
ptr is an opaque user pointer passed to the callback.
Returns 0 on success and 1 on error (per C++ wrapper documentation). Callback return controls traversal (continue/stop/error via TSK_WALK_RET_ENUM).

functions.name: tsk_vs_part_read
functions.signature: ssize_t tsk_vs_part_read(const TSK_VS_PART_INFO * a_vs_part, TSK_OFF_T a_off, char *buf, size_t len);
functions.description: Reads data starting at a byte offset relative to the start of the specified partition into the buffer.
requirements: a_vs_part must be a valid partition descriptor from the open VS.
a_off is a byte offset relative to the start of the partition (non-negative).
buf must point to a writable buffer of at least len bytes.
len is the number of bytes to read.
Returns number of bytes read or -1 on error. Behavior when reading beyond partition bounds is not documented (may truncate or error).

functions.name: tsk_vs_part_read_block
functions.signature: ssize_t tsk_vs_part_read_block(const TSK_VS_PART_INFO * a_vs_part, TSK_DADDR_T a_addr, char *buf, size_t len);
functions.description: Reads one or more blocks from the partition at a block address relative to the start of the partition into the buffer.
requirements: a_vs_part must be a valid partition descriptor from the open VS.
a_addr is a sector/block address relative to the start of the partition.
buf must point to a writable buffer of at least len bytes.
len must be a multiple of the VS block_size (per class documentation referencing this function).
Returns number of bytes read or -1 on error.

functions.name: tsk_vs_part_walk_cpp_c_cb
functions.signature: TSK_WALK_RET_ENUM tsk_vs_part_walk_cpp_c_cb(TSK_VS_INFO * a_vs, const TSK_VS_PART_INFO * a_vs_part, void *a_ptr);
functions.description: Internal bridge callback that allows a C++ partition-walk callback to be invoked from the C tsk_vs_part_walk() API.
requirements: a_vs must be a valid TSK_VS_INFO*.
a_vs_part is the current partition (const).
a_ptr should point to a TSK_VS_PART_WALK_CPP_DATA structure as set by TskVsInfo::vsPartWalk.
Return value must be a valid TSK_WALK_RET_ENUM to control traversal.

functions.name: TskVsPartInfo::read
functions.signature: ssize_t TskVsPartInfo::read(TSK_OFF_T a_off, char *a_buf, size_t a_len)
functions.description: Reads data starting at a byte offset relative to the start of the partition into the provided buffer. Thin wrapper around tsk_vs_part_read().
requirements: This object must wrap a non-NULL TSK_VS_PART_INFO (constructed with a valid pointer).
a_buf must point to a writable buffer of at least a_len bytes.
Returns number of bytes read or -1 on error. If the underlying C pointer is NULL, returns 0.

functions.name: TskVsPartInfo::readBlock
functions.signature: ssize_t TskVsPartInfo::readBlock(TSK_DADDR_T a_addr, char *a_buf, size_t a_len)
functions.description: Reads one or more blocks from the partition at the given block address into the buffer. Wrapper around tsk_vs_part_read_block().
requirements: This object must wrap a non-NULL TSK_VS_PART_INFO.
a_len must be a multiple of the volume system block_size.
a_buf must point to a writable buffer of at least a_len bytes.
Returns number of bytes read or -1 on error. If the underlying C pointer is NULL, returns 0.

functions.name: TskVsPartInfo::getStart
functions.description: Returns the sector offset of the start of the partition.
requirements: This object must wrap a non-NULL TSK_VS_PART_INFO. If NULL, returns 0.

functions.name: TskVsPartInfo::getLen
functions.description: Returns the number of sectors in the partition.
requirements: This object must wrap a non-NULL TSK_VS_PART_INFO. If NULL, returns 0.

functions.name: TskVsPartInfo::getDesc
functions.description: Returns the UTF-8 description of the partition (VS-type specific), or NULL if unavailable.
requirements: This object must wrap a non-NULL TSK_VS_PART_INFO. If NULL, returns NULL.
Caller must not free or modify the returned string pointer.

functions.name: TskVsPartInfo::getTableNum
functions.description: Returns the table address identifier that describes this partition.
requirements: This object must wrap a non-NULL TSK_VS_PART_INFO. If NULL, returns 0.

functions.name: TskVsPartInfo::getSlotNum
functions.description: Returns the table entry index (slot) that describes this partition.
requirements: This object must wrap a non-NULL TSK_VS_PART_INFO. If NULL, returns 0.

functions.name: TskVsPartInfo::getAddr
functions.description: Returns the address (index) of this partition within the volume system.
requirements: This object must wrap a non-NULL TSK_VS_PART_INFO. If NULL, returns 0.

functions.name: TskVsPartInfo::getFlags
functions.description: Returns the flags for this partition (ALLOC, UNALLOC, META, etc.).
requirements: This object must wrap a non-NULL TSK_VS_PART_INFO. If NULL, returns 0 cast to TSK_VS_PART_FLAG_ENUM.

functions.name: TskVsInfo::vsPartWalk
functions.signature: uint8_t TskVsInfo::vsPartWalk(TSK_PNUM_T a_start, TSK_PNUM_T a_last, TSK_VS_PART_FLAG_ENUM a_flags, TSK_VS_PART_WALK_CPP_CB a_action, void *a_ptr)
functions.description: Walks partitions from a_start to a_last (inclusive) filtering by flags and invokes the provided C++ callback for each. Internally bridges to tsk_vs_part_walk() via tsk_vs_part_walk_cpp_c_cb.
requirements: This object must encapsulate a valid TSK_VS_INFO* (typically via open()).
a_action must be a valid callback; it will be invoked for each visited partition.
a_ptr is an opaque user pointer passed to the callback.
Returns 0 on success and 1 on error (per wrapper).

functions.name: TskVsInfo::open
functions.signature: uint8_t TskVsInfo::open(TskImgInfo * a_imgInfo, TSK_DADDR_T a_offset, TSK_VS_TYPE_ENUM a_type)
functions.description: Opens a volume system on the provided image at the given byte offset, using the specified type or auto-detection. Wraps tsk_vs_open().
requirements: a_imgInfo must point to a valid, already-open TskImgInfo.
a_offset is a byte offset from the start of the image.
a_type is a TSK_VS_TYPE_ENUM (TSK_VS_TYPE_DETECT allowed).
On success, returns 0 and the object owns the underlying handle until close(). On failure, returns 1.

functions.name: TskVsInfo::readBlock
functions.signature: ssize_t TskVsInfo::readBlock(TSK_DADDR_T a_addr, char *a_buf, size_t a_len)
functions.description: Reads one or more blocks from the volume system at the given block address into the buffer. Wraps tsk_vs_read_block().
requirements: This object must encapsulate a valid TSK_VS_INFO*.
a_len must be a multiple of the VS block_size.
a_buf must point to a writable buffer of at least a_len bytes.
Returns number of bytes read or -1 on error. If the underlying C pointer is NULL, returns 0.

functions.name: TskVsInfo::close
functions.description: Closes the open volume system if this object opened it, releasing resources. Wraps tsk_vs_close().
requirements: Safe to call multiple times; after close(), the internal handle is set to NULL.
Only closes if the object previously opened the VS (tracked by m_opened).

functions.name: TskVsInfo::getOffset
functions.description: Returns the byte offset where the volume system starts in the disk image.
requirements: Object must encapsulate a valid TSK_VS_INFO*. If NULL, returns 0.

functions.name: TskVsInfo::getBlockSize
functions.description: Returns the volume system block size in bytes.
requirements: Object must encapsulate a valid TSK_VS_INFO*. If NULL, returns 0.

functions.name: TskVsInfo::getPartCount
functions.description: Returns the number of partitions in the volume system.
requirements: Object must encapsulate a valid TSK_VS_INFO*. If NULL, returns 0.

functions.name: TskVsInfo::getPart
functions.description: Returns a newly allocated wrapper for the partition at the given 0-based index. Internally calls tsk_vs_part_get() and wraps the returned C struct.
requirements: Object must encapsulate a valid TSK_VS_INFO*.
a_idx is 0-based; out-of-range will result in wrapping a NULL pointer.
Caller is responsible for freeing the returned TskVsPartInfo object. The underlying C struct is owned by the VS and must not be freed by the caller.

functions.name: TskVsInfo::getImgInfo
functions.description: Returns a newly allocated wrapper for the parent image object of this volume system.
requirements: Object must encapsulate a valid TSK_VS_INFO*. If NULL, returns 0.
Caller is responsible for freeing the returned TskImgInfo object.

functions.name: TskVsInfo::getVsType
functions.description: Returns the type of volume system/media management for this handle.
requirements: Object must encapsulate a valid TSK_VS_INFO*. If NULL, returns 0 cast to TSK_VS_TYPE_ENUM.

functions.name: TskVsInfo::typeToId
functions.description: Static helper that parses a VS type string into its enum identifier. Wraps tsk_vs_type_toid().
requirements: a_str must be a valid, null-terminated TSK_TCHAR string.

functions.name: TskVsInfo::typePrint
functions.description: Static helper that prints supported VS type names to the given FILE stream. Wraps tsk_vs_type_print().
requirements: a_hFile must be a valid, open FILE* for writing.

functions.name: TskVsInfo::typeSupported
functions.description: Static helper that returns a bitmask of supported VS types. Wraps tsk_vs_type_supported().
requirements: No arguments.

functions.name: TskVsInfo::typeToName
functions.description: Static helper that returns the string name of a VS type. Wraps tsk_vs_type_toname().
requirements: a_type must be a valid TSK_VS_TYPE_ENUM.
Returned string is const; do not modify or free.

functions.name: TskVsInfo::typeToDesc
functions.description: Static helper that returns the string description of a VS type. Wraps tsk_vs_type_todesc().
requirements: a_type must be a valid TSK_VS_TYPE_ENUM.
Returned string is const; do not modify or free.

functions.name: tsk_fs_block_free
functions.description: Frees a TSK_FS_BLOCK previously obtained (e.g., via tsk_fs_block_get or tsk_fs_block_get_flag). Intended to release internal allocations associated with a block handle.
requirements: a_fs_block may be NULL (safe to call in many C APIs, but behavior not explicitly stated here)
a_fs_block must be a valid TSK_FS_BLOCK previously allocated/returned by this library
Do not use a_fs_block after this call

functions.name: tsk_fs_block_get
functions.signature: extern TSK_FS_BLOCK *tsk_fs_block_get(TSK_FS_INFO * fs, TSK_FS_BLOCK * fs_block, TSK_DADDR_T addr);
functions.description: Returns a TSK_FS_BLOCK for the specified file system block address. If fs_block is NULL, a new block handle is allocated; otherwise the provided handle is populated.
requirements: fs must be a valid, open TSK_FS_INFO
addr must be within the file system’s valid block address range [fs->first_block, fs->last_block_act] (not explicitly stated, but implied)
If fs_block is non-NULL, it must point to a valid TSK_FS_BLOCK to be reused
Caller must free the returned/updated TSK_FS_BLOCK with tsk_fs_block_free when done

functions.name: tsk_fs_block_get_flag
functions.signature: extern TSK_FS_BLOCK *tsk_fs_block_get_flag(TSK_FS_INFO * a_fs, TSK_FS_BLOCK * a_fs_block, TSK_DADDR_T a_addr, TSK_FS_BLOCK_FLAG_ENUM a_flags);
functions.description: Returns a TSK_FS_BLOCK for the specified address, allowing the caller to specify expected flags (e.g., allocation metadata) to be set on the returned block.
requirements: a_fs must be a valid, open TSK_FS_INFO
a_addr should be a valid block address
If a_fs_block is non-NULL it must be an existing TSK_FS_BLOCK to reuse; otherwise a new one is allocated
a_flags is used to set/indicate properties on the returned block; valid values are from TSK_FS_BLOCK_FLAG_ENUM
Caller must free the returned/updated TSK_FS_BLOCK with tsk_fs_block_free

functions.name: tsk_fs_block_walk
functions.signature: extern uint8_t tsk_fs_block_walk(TSK_FS_INFO * a_fs, TSK_DADDR_T a_start_blk, TSK_DADDR_T a_end_blk, TSK_FS_BLOCK_WALK_FLAG_ENUM a_flags, TSK_FS_BLOCK_WALK_CB a_action, void *a_ptr);
functions.description: Walks file system blocks in the inclusive range [a_start_blk, a_end_blk], invoking a_action for blocks matching the selection flags (allocated/unallocated, content/meta, etc.).
requirements: a_fs must be a valid, open TSK_FS_INFO
a_start_blk and a_end_blk denote a valid range; start should be <= end and within the FS address space
a_flags must be a combination of TSK_FS_BLOCK_WALK_FLAG_ENUM values
a_action must be a valid callback of type TSK_FS_BLOCK_WALK_CB that returns a TSK_WALK_RET_ENUM to control iteration
a_ptr is an opaque user pointer passed through to the callback
If AONLY flag is set, callback must not dereference content buffer (data may be omitted)

functions.name: tsk_fs_attr_run_free
functions.description: Frees a TSK_FS_ATTR_RUN (or list of runs) used to describe non-resident data extents of an attribute.
requirements: Argument must be a TSK_FS_ATTR_RUN previously allocated/managed by this library
After freeing, the pointer must not be used

functions.name: tsk_fs_attr_walk
functions.signature: extern uint8_t tsk_fs_attr_walk(const TSK_FS_ATTR * a_fs_attr, TSK_FS_FILE_WALK_FLAG_ENUM a_flags, TSK_FS_FILE_WALK_CB a_action, void *a_ptr);
functions.description: Walks the content of a specific file attribute, invoking a callback with chunks of data (up to fs->block_size) based on flags (e.g., include slack or sparse).
requirements: a_fs_attr must point to a valid attribute
a_flags must be from TSK_FS_FILE_WALK_FLAG_ENUM
a_action must be a valid callback of type TSK_FS_FILE_WALK_CB returning TSK_WALK_RET_ENUM
If AONLY flag is set, callback should not use a_buf (no content provided)
For sparse/compressed attributes, the a_addr in callback may be zero or not meaningful (as noted)

functions.name: tsk_fs_meta_walk
functions.signature: extern uint8_t tsk_fs_meta_walk(TSK_FS_INFO * a_fs, TSK_INUM_T a_start, TSK_INUM_T a_end, TSK_FS_META_FLAG_ENUM a_flags, TSK_FS_META_WALK_CB a_cb, void *a_ptr);
functions.description: Walks metadata (inodes) in the range [a_start, a_end], invoking a callback for entries that match the flags (e.g., allocated, unallocated, orphan).
requirements: a_fs must be a valid, open TSK_FS_INFO
a_start <= a_end and within valid metadata addresses [fs->first_inum, fs->last_inum]
a_flags must be a combination of TSK_FS_META_FLAG_ENUM values
a_cb must be a valid callback of type TSK_FS_META_WALK_CB returning TSK_WALK_RET_ENUM
a_ptr is an opaque user pointer passed through to the callback

functions.name: tsk_fs_meta_make_ls
functions.signature: extern uint8_t tsk_fs_meta_make_ls(const TSK_FS_META * a_fs_meta, char *a_buf, size_t a_len);
functions.description: Formats a Unix-style permissions string (like ls -l) based on the metadata, writing it into a_buf.
requirements: a_fs_meta must be a valid metadata pointer
a_buf must point to writable memory
a_len must be >= 12 bytes (explicitly documented)
Caller must ensure buffer is large enough to hold the resulting string

functions.name: tsk_fs_dir_open_meta
functions.description: Opens a directory by metadata address and returns a directory handle for enumerating its entries.
requirements: a_fs must be a valid, open TSK_FS_INFO
a_addr must refer to a directory inode within the file system
Returned TSK_FS_DIR must be closed with tsk_fs_dir_close

functions.name: tsk_fs_dir_open
functions.description: Opens a directory by path (UTF-8) and returns a directory handle for enumerating its entries.
requirements: a_fs must be a valid, open TSK_FS_INFO
a_dir must be a valid, absolute or relative path interpretable in the file system
Returned TSK_FS_DIR must be closed with tsk_fs_dir_close

functions.name: tsk_fs_dir_walk
functions.signature: extern uint8_t tsk_fs_dir_walk(TSK_FS_INFO * a_fs, TSK_INUM_T a_inode, TSK_FS_DIR_WALK_FLAG_ENUM a_flags, TSK_FS_DIR_WALK_CB a_action, void *a_ptr);
functions.description: Walks the entries in a directory (and optionally recurses) invoking a callback for each entry matching selection flags (allocated/unallocated, no-orphan, etc.).
requirements: a_fs must be a valid, open TSK_FS_INFO
a_inode must refer to a directory
a_flags must be from TSK_FS_DIR_WALK_FLAG_ENUM; RECURSE controls recursion; NOORPHAN excludes the orphan dir
a_action must be a valid callback returning TSK_WALK_RET_ENUM
a_ptr is an opaque user pointer passed to the callback

functions.name: tsk_fs_dir_getsize
functions.description: Returns the number of entries (files/subdirectories) currently available from an open directory handle.
requirements: Argument must be a valid, open TSK_FS_DIR

functions.name: tsk_fs_dir_get
functions.description: Returns a TSK_FS_FILE handle for the directory entry at the given index.
requirements: First argument must be a valid, open TSK_FS_DIR
Index must be less than tsk_fs_dir_getsize(dir)
Returned TSK_FS_FILE should be closed with tsk_fs_file_close when no longer needed

functions.name: tsk_fs_dir_get2
functions.signature: extern TSK_FS_FILE *tsk_fs_dir_get2(const TSK_FS_DIR *, size_t, size_t load_attributes);
functions.description: Returns a TSK_FS_FILE handle for the directory entry at the given index, with an option controlling attribute loading (load_attributes).
requirements: First argument must be a valid, open TSK_FS_DIR
Index must be within the directory size
load_attributes influences attribute loading; exact semantics are not documented here
Returned TSK_FS_FILE should be closed with tsk_fs_file_close when done

functions.name: tsk_fs_dir_get_name
functions.signature: extern const TSK_FS_NAME *tsk_fs_dir_get_name(const TSK_FS_DIR * a_fs_dir, size_t a_idx);
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the TSK_FS_NAME (name record) for the directory entry at index a_idx.
requirements: a_fs_dir must be a valid TSK_FS_DIR
a_idx must be within bounds of the directory entry list
Returned pointer is owned by the directory handle; do not free; lifetime tied to TSK_FS_DIR

functions.name: tsk_fs_dir_close
functions.description: Closes a directory handle previously opened by tsk_fs_dir_open or tsk_fs_dir_open_meta and releases associated resources.
requirements: Argument must be a TSK_FS_DIR obtained from this library
Do not use the directory handle or any of its returned internal pointers after closing

functions.name: tsk_fs_path2inum
functions.signature: extern int8_t tsk_fs_path2inum(TSK_FS_INFO * a_fs, const char *a_path, TSK_INUM_T * a_result, TSK_FS_NAME * a_fs_name);
functions.description: Looks up a path and returns the corresponding metadata address (inode). Optionally returns a copy of name details.
requirements: a_fs must be a valid, open TSK_FS_INFO
a_path must be a valid UTF-8 path in the file system namespace
a_result must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the inode
a_fs_name may be NULL if details are not desired
Return values: -1 on system error, 0 if found, 1 if not found (per documentation in C++ wrapper)

functions.name: tsk_fs_file_close
functions.description: Closes a file handle previously obtained from the directory APIs or the file open APIs and releases associated resources.
requirements: a_fs_file must be a TSK_FS_FILE obtained from this library
Do not use a_fs_file after closing

functions.name: tsk_fs_file_open
functions.signature: extern TSK_FS_FILE *tsk_fs_file_open(TSK_FS_INFO * a_fs, TSK_FS_FILE * a_fs_file, const char *a_path);
functions.description: Opens a file by path (UTF-8). If a_fs_file is NULL, a new file object is allocated; otherwise the given object is populated.
requirements: a_fs must be a valid, open TSK_FS_INFO
a_path must be a valid path to a file
If a_fs_file is non-NULL it must point to a valid TSK_FS_FILE to reuse
Returned/updated file handle must be closed with tsk_fs_file_close

functions.name: tsk_fs_file_open_meta
functions.signature: extern TSK_FS_FILE *tsk_fs_file_open_meta(TSK_FS_INFO * fs, TSK_FS_FILE * fs_file, TSK_INUM_T addr);
functions.description: Opens a file by metadata address (inode). If fs_file is NULL, a new file object is allocated; otherwise the given one is filled. This does not resolve the filename.
requirements: fs must be a valid, open TSK_FS_INFO
addr must be a valid inode address for a file or directory
If fs_file is non-NULL it must be a valid TSK_FS_FILE to reuse
Returned/updated file handle must be closed with tsk_fs_file_close

functions.name: tsk_fs_file_read
functions.signature: extern ssize_t tsk_fs_file_read(TSK_FS_FILE *, TSK_OFF_T, char *, size_t, TSK_FS_FILE_READ_FLAG_ENUM);
functions.description: Reads data from the default attribute of an open file into a buffer, optionally allowing reads into slack space.
requirements: First argument must be a valid, open TSK_FS_FILE
Offset must be >= 0
Buffer pointer must be writable
Length specifies number of bytes to read; may be 0
Flags are from TSK_FS_FILE_READ_FLAG_ENUM (e.g., SLACK, NOID)
Returns number of bytes read or -1 on error (including offset beyond EOF)

functions.name: tsk_fs_file_read_type
functions.signature: extern ssize_t tsk_fs_file_read(TSK_FS_FILE *, TSK_FS_ATTR_TYPE_ENUM, uint16_t, TSK_OFF_T, char *, size_t, TSK_FS_FILE_READ_FLAG_ENUM);
functions.description: Reads data from a specific attribute (type/id) of an open file into a buffer.
requirements: First argument must be a valid, open TSK_FS_FILE
Attribute type must be from TSK_FS_ATTR_TYPE_ENUM
Attribute id selects a specific attribute (0 may mean default depending on flags)
Offset >= 0; buffer writable; length bytes requested
Flags from TSK_FS_FILE_READ_FLAG_ENUM
Returns bytes read or -1 on error

functions.name: tsk_fs_file_attr_get
functions.description: Returns the default attribute of a file (typically the file content attribute).
requirements: a_fs_file must be a valid TSK_FS_FILE
Returned pointer is owned by the TSK_FS_FILE; do not free; lifetime tied to the file handle

functions.name: tsk_fs_file_attr_getsize
functions.description: Returns the number of attributes attached to the file.
requirements: a_fs_file must be a valid TSK_FS_FILE

functions.name: tsk_fs_file_attr_get_idx
functions.signature: extern const TSK_FS_ATTR *tsk_fs_file_attr_get_idx(TSK_FS_FILE * a_fs_file, int a_idx);
functions.description: Returns the attribute at the given 0-based index in the file’s attribute list.
requirements: a_fs_file must be valid
a_idx must be within [0, tsk_fs_file_attr_getsize(file))
Returned pointer is owned by the file; do not free

functions.name: tsk_fs_file_attr_get_type
functions.signature: extern const TSK_FS_ATTR *tsk_fs_file_attr_get_type(TSK_FS_FILE * a_fs_file, TSK_FS_ATTR_TYPE_ENUM, uint16_t, uint8_t);
functions.description: Returns the attribute matching the given type and id. The last parameter indicates whether the ID is used.
requirements: a_fs_file must be valid
Type must be from TSK_FS_ATTR_TYPE_ENUM
Id is a 16-bit attribute identifier; the id_used flag indicates whether to use it
Returned pointer is owned by the file; do not free

functions.name: tsk_fs_file_attr_get_id
functions.description: Returns the attribute with the specified id.
requirements: a_fs_file must be valid
Returned pointer is owned by the file; do not free

functions.name: tsk_fs_file_walk
functions.signature: extern uint8_t tsk_fs_file_walk(TSK_FS_FILE * a_fs_file, TSK_FS_FILE_WALK_FLAG_ENUM a_flags, TSK_FS_FILE_WALK_CB a_action, void *a_ptr);
functions.description: Walks the default attribute of a file and invokes a callback with chunks of content based on the provided flags (e.g., include slack, no sparse).
requirements: a_fs_file must be a valid open file
a_flags must be from TSK_FS_FILE_WALK_FLAG_ENUM
a_action must be a valid callback returning TSK_WALK_RET_ENUM
If AONLY flag is set, callback must not assume a_buf contains content
For SPARSE/COMP data the a_addr may be not meaningful

functions.name: tsk_fs_file_walk_type
functions.signature: extern uint8_t tsk_fs_file_walk(TSK_FS_FILE * a_fs_file, TSK_FS_ATTR_TYPE_ENUM a_type, uint16_t a_id, TSK_FS_FILE_WALK_FLAG_ENUM a_flags, TSK_FS_FILE_WALK_CB a_action, void *a_ptr);
functions.description: Walks a specific attribute (type/id) of a file and invokes a callback with content chunks based on flags.
requirements: a_fs_file must be valid
a_type and a_id select the attribute; a_id may be ignored depending on flags
a_flags from TSK_FS_FILE_WALK_FLAG_ENUM
a_action must be valid and return TSK_WALK_RET_ENUM

functions.name: tsk_fs_attr_read
functions.signature: extern ssize_t tsk_fs_attr_read(const TSK_FS_ATTR * a_fs_attr, TSK_OFF_T a_offset, char *a_buf, size_t a_len, TSK_FS_FILE_READ_FLAG_ENUM a_flags);
functions.description: Reads data from a specific attribute (resident or non-resident) into a buffer. Missing runs are returned as zeros.
requirements: a_fs_attr must be valid
a_offset >= 0
a_buf must be writable and at least a_len bytes
a_flags from TSK_FS_FILE_READ_FLAG_ENUM
Returns bytes read or -1 on error (including offset past end)

functions.name: tsk_fs_file_get_owner_sid
functions.description: Retrieves the owner SID string for a file (primarily for NTFS). The output is a string returned via char **.
requirements: First argument must be a valid TSK_FS_FILE
Second argument must be a non-NULL char **; allocation/ownership semantics are not specified in this header (unknown)
Function returns 0 on success and 1 on error (convention used elsewhere; exact codes not explicitly stated)

functions.name: tsk_fs_file_hash_calc
functions.description: Calculates selected hash(es) (MD5, SHA1, etc.) of a file’s content and stores digests in TSK_FS_HASH_RESULTS per the flags.
requirements: First argument must be a valid TSK_FS_FILE
Second argument must point to a valid TSK_FS_HASH_RESULTS to receive results
Third argument is a bitmask of TSK_BASE_HASH_ENUM indicating which hashes to compute

functions.name: tsk_fs_open_img
functions.description: Opens a file system at a given byte offset in a disk image layer and returns a handle for analysis.
requirements: First argument must be a valid TSK_IMG_INFO
Offset is the byte offset of the FS start relative to the image
Type is a TSK_FS_TYPE_ENUM value (or TSK_FS_TYPE_DETECT for autodetect)
Returned TSK_FS_INFO must be closed with tsk_fs_close

functions.name: tsk_fs_open_vol
functions.description: Opens a file system within a specific volume/partition and returns a handle.
requirements: First argument must be a valid TSK_VS_PART_INFO
Type is a TSK_FS_TYPE_ENUM (or DETECT)
Returned TSK_FS_INFO must be closed with tsk_fs_close

functions.name: tsk_fs_open_pool
functions.description: Opens a file system within a pool (e.g., storage pool) context at a given pool-relative address.
requirements: First argument must be a valid TSK_POOL_INFO
Second argument is a pool-relative address (TSK_DADDR_T)
Type is TSK_FS_TYPE_ENUM (or DETECT)
Returned TSK_FS_INFO must be closed with tsk_fs_close

functions.name: tsk_fs_open_img_decrypt
functions.signature: extern TSK_FS_INFO *tsk_fs_open_img_decrypt(TSK_IMG_INFO *, TSK_OFF_T, TSK_FS_TYPE_ENUM, const char * password);
functions.description: Opens a (potentially encrypted) file system at a given image offset, using the supplied password for decryption if required.
requirements: Valid TSK_IMG_INFO and offset
Type is TSK_FS_TYPE_ENUM (or DETECT)
password may be NULL or a UTF-8 string depending on FS/encryption (details not specified)
Returned handle must be closed with tsk_fs_close

functions.name: tsk_fs_open_vol_decrypt
functions.signature: extern TSK_FS_INFO *tsk_fs_open_vol_decrypt(const TSK_VS_PART_INFO *, TSK_FS_TYPE_ENUM, const char * password);
functions.description: Opens a (potentially encrypted) file system in a given volume using the provided password.
requirements: Valid TSK_VS_PART_INFO
Type is TSK_FS_TYPE_ENUM (or DETECT)
password may be required by the underlying FS/encryption (details not specified)
Close with tsk_fs_close

functions.name: tsk_fs_open_pool_decrypt
functions.signature: extern TSK_FS_INFO *tsk_fs_open_pool_decrypt(const TSK_POOL_INFO *, TSK_DADDR_T, TSK_FS_TYPE_ENUM, const char * password);
functions.description: Opens a (potentially encrypted) file system in a pool at a given address, using a password if needed.
requirements: Valid TSK_POOL_INFO and pool-relative address
Type is TSK_FS_TYPE_ENUM (or DETECT)
password usage depends on FS/encryption (unspecified)
Close with tsk_fs_close

functions.name: tsk_fs_close
functions.description: Closes a file system handle and releases associated resources.
requirements: Argument must be a TSK_FS_INFO obtained from this library
Do not use the handle after closing

functions.name: tsk_fs_type_toid_utf8
functions.description: Parses a UTF-8 string naming a file system type and returns its TSK_FS_TYPE_ENUM ID, or UNSUPP if unknown.
requirements: Argument must be a valid C string (UTF-8) naming a FS type

functions.name: tsk_fs_type_toid
functions.description: Parses a TSK_TCHAR string naming a file system type and returns its TSK_FS_TYPE_ENUM ID, or UNSUPP if unknown.
requirements: Argument must be a valid TSK_TCHAR string naming a FS type

functions.name: tsk_fs_type_print
functions.description: Prints the supported file system types to the given FILE stream.
requirements: Argument must be a valid FILE* opened for writing or stdout/stderr

functions.name: tsk_fs_type_toname
functions.description: Returns the string name for a given TSK_FS_TYPE_ENUM value.
requirements: Argument must be a valid TSK_FS_TYPE_ENUM value; returns NULL on error/unknown

functions.name: tsk_fs_type_supported
functions.description: Returns a bitmask of supported file system types (bits correspond to TSK_FS_TYPE_ENUM).

functions.name: tsk_fs_get_encryption_description
functions.signature: extern void tsk_fs_get_encryption_description(TSK_FS_INFO* a_fs_info, char* a_desc, size_t a_descLen);
functions.description: Writes a human-readable description of the file system’s encryption (if any) into the provided buffer.
requirements: a_fs_info must be a valid TSK_FS_INFO
a_desc must be a writable buffer
a_descLen must specify the buffer size; function will not write beyond it

functions.name: tsk_fs_read
functions.signature: extern ssize_t tsk_fs_read(TSK_FS_INFO * a_fs, TSK_OFF_T a_off, char *a_buf, size_t a_len);
functions.description: Reads arbitrary bytes from within the file system (relative to the FS start) into a buffer.
requirements: a_fs must be valid
a_off is a byte offset >= 0 within the FS address space
