a_buf must be writable and at least a_len bytes
Returns bytes read or -1 on error

functions.name: tsk_fs_read_decrypt
functions.signature: extern ssize_t tsk_fs_read_decrypt(TSK_FS_INFO * a_fs, TSK_OFF_T a_off, char *a_buf, size_t a_len, TSK_DADDR_T crypto_id);
functions.description: Reads arbitrary bytes from within the file system with decryption context specified by crypto_id.
requirements: a_fs must be valid and decryption-capable
a_off >= 0; a_buf writable; a_len is byte count
crypto_id identifies the decryption IV/start (as documented in structures)
Returns bytes read or -1 on error

functions.name: tsk_fs_read_block
functions.signature: extern ssize_t tsk_fs_read_block(TSK_FS_INFO * a_fs, TSK_DADDR_T a_addr, char *a_buf, size_t a_len);
functions.description: Reads one or more file system blocks starting at a_addr into a buffer.
requirements: a_fs must be valid
a_addr is a starting block address within the file system
a_buf must be writable; a_len must be a multiple of the block size (explicitly documented in C++ wrapper)
Returns bytes read or -1 on error

functions.name: tsk_fs_read_block_decrypt
functions.signature: extern ssize_t tsk_fs_read_block_decrypt(TSK_FS_INFO * a_fs, TSK_DADDR_T a_addr, char *a_buf, size_t a_len, TSK_DADDR_T crypto_id);
functions.description: Reads one or more blocks with decryption starting at a_addr, writing into a_buf.
requirements: a_fs must be valid and support decryption
a_addr must be a valid block address
a_len must be a multiple of block size
crypto_id supplies encryption context (e.g., for XTS IV)
Returns bytes read or -1 on error

functions.name: tsk_fs_blkcalc
functions.signature: extern int8_t tsk_fs_blkcalc(TSK_FS_INFO * fs, TSK_FS_BLKCALC_FLAG_ENUM flags, TSK_DADDR_T cnt);
functions.description: Library routine used by command-line tools to calculate and report on block ranges/counts based on flags (e.g., dd, blkls, slack).
requirements: fs must be valid
flags from TSK_FS_BLKCALC_FLAG_ENUM
cnt is a block count parameter; exact semantics depend on flag

functions.name: tsk_fs_blkcat
functions.signature: extern uint8_t tsk_fs_blkcat(TSK_FS_INFO * fs, TSK_FS_BLKCAT_FLAG_ENUM flags, TSK_DADDR_T addr, TSK_DADDR_T read_num_units);
functions.description: Library routine used by command-line tools to print or output block contents in various formats (hex, ascii, html, stat).
requirements: fs must be valid
flags from TSK_FS_BLKCAT_FLAG_ENUM
addr is starting block address
read_num_units is the number of units (blocks) to read/output

functions.name: tsk_fs_blkls
functions.signature: extern uint8_t tsk_fs_blkls(TSK_FS_INFO * fs, TSK_FS_BLKLS_FLAG_ENUM lclflags, TSK_DADDR_T bstart, TSK_DADDR_T bend, TSK_FS_BLOCK_WALK_FLAG_ENUM flags);
functions.description: Library routine used by command-line tools to list or concatenate block data in a range, with options to include slack or produce listings.
requirements: fs must be valid
lclflags from TSK_FS_BLKLS_FLAG_ENUM
bstart..bend define a block range
flags select allocated/unallocated/meta/content blocks (TSK_FS_BLOCK_WALK_FLAG_ENUM)

functions.name: tsk_fs_blkstat
functions.signature: extern uint8_t tsk_fs_blkstat(TSK_FS_INFO * fs, TSK_DADDR_T addr);
functions.description: Prints or returns status information about a specific block (used by blkstat tool).
requirements: fs must be valid
addr must be a valid block address

functions.name: tsk_fs_ffind
functions.signature: extern uint8_t tsk_fs_ffind(TSK_FS_INFO * fs, TSK_FS_FFIND_FLAG_ENUM lclflags, TSK_INUM_T inode, TSK_FS_ATTR_TYPE_ENUM type, uint8_t type_used, uint16_t id, uint8_t id_used, TSK_FS_DIR_WALK_FLAG_ENUM flags);
functions.description: Finds names/paths that reference a given inode and prints/reports them per flags (used by ffind tool).
requirements: fs must be valid
lclflags from TSK_FS_FFIND_FLAG_ENUM
inode is the target metadata address
type and id filters are used only if corresponding *_used flags are set
flags control directory walk behavior (TSK_FS_DIR_WALK_FLAG_ENUM)

functions.name: tsk_fs_fls
functions.signature: extern uint8_t tsk_fs_fls(TSK_FS_INFO * fs, TSK_FS_FLS_FLAG_ENUM lclflags, TSK_INUM_T inode, TSK_FS_DIR_WALK_FLAG_ENUM flags, const TSK_TCHAR * pre, int32_t skew);
functions.description: Lists directory contents (like fls tool) starting at a given inode, with formatting and filtering options.
requirements: fs must be valid
lclflags from TSK_FS_FLS_FLAG_ENUM (e.g., LONG, FILE, DIR, FULL, HASH)
inode specifies start directory
flags control recursion and inclusion (TSK_FS_DIR_WALK_FLAG_ENUM)
pre is a path prefix to print, may be NULL
skew is a time skew (seconds) applied to printed times

functions.name: tsk_fs_icat
functions.signature: extern uint8_t tsk_fs_icat(TSK_FS_INFO * fs, TSK_INUM_T inum, TSK_FS_ATTR_TYPE_ENUM type, uint8_t type_used, uint16_t id, uint8_t id_used, TSK_FS_FILE_WALK_FLAG_ENUM flags);
functions.description: Outputs/prints the content of a file (like icat tool) specified by inode and optional attribute type/id, honoring walk flags.
requirements: fs must be valid
inum is the target inode
type and id filters are used only if corresponding *_used flags are set
flags from TSK_FS_FILE_WALK_FLAG_ENUM

functions.name: tsk_fs_ifind_path
functions.signature: extern int8_t tsk_fs_ifind_path(TSK_FS_INFO * fs, TSK_TCHAR * path, TSK_INUM_T * result);
functions.description: Parses a path and finds the corresponding inode number, writing it to result.
requirements: fs must be valid
path must be a valid TSK_TCHAR path
result must be non-NULL to receive the inode
Returns 0 on success and 1 on error or if not an inode (per pattern used in wrapper; exact return not fully specified)

functions.name: tsk_fs_ifind_data
functions.signature: extern uint8_t tsk_fs_ifind_data(TSK_FS_INFO * fs, TSK_FS_IFIND_FLAG_ENUM flags, TSK_DADDR_T blk);
functions.description: Finds file(s) that reference a given data block (used by ifind tool) according to flags.
requirements: fs must be valid
flags from TSK_FS_IFIND_FLAG_ENUM
blk is a data block address within the FS

functions.name: tsk_fs_ifind_par
functions.signature: extern uint8_t tsk_fs_ifind_par(TSK_FS_INFO * fs, TSK_FS_IFIND_FLAG_ENUM flags, TSK_INUM_T par);
functions.description: Finds child entries of the given parent inode or resolves parent relationships (used by ifind tool) according to flags.
requirements: fs must be valid
flags from TSK_FS_IFIND_FLAG_ENUM
par is a parent inode address

functions.name: tsk_fs_ils
functions.signature: extern uint8_t tsk_fs_ils(TSK_FS_INFO * fs, TSK_FS_ILS_FLAG_ENUM lclflags, TSK_INUM_T istart, TSK_INUM_T ilast, TSK_FS_META_FLAG_ENUM flags, int32_t skew, const TSK_TCHAR * img);
functions.description: Lists metadata (inodes) based on allocation/link state and time options (used by ils tool).
requirements: fs must be valid
lclflags from TSK_FS_ILS_FLAG_ENUM (OPEN, MAC, LINK, UNLINK)
istart..ilast is the inode range
flags select inode status (TSK_FS_META_FLAG_ENUM)
skew is clock skew to apply (seconds)
img is an image path string used in output (may be NULL)

functions.name: tsk_fs_parse_inum
functions.signature: extern int tsk_fs_parse_inum(const TSK_TCHAR * str, TSK_INUM_T *, TSK_FS_ATTR_TYPE_ENUM *, uint8_t *, uint16_t *, uint8_t *);

functions.name: APFSFSCompat::APFSFSCompat
functions.signature: APFSFSCompat(TSK_IMG_INFO* img_info, const TSK_POOL_INFO* pool_info, apfs_block_num vol_block, const char* pass = "")
functions.description: Constructs an APFSFSCompat instance that adapts an APFS volume to The Sleuth Kit (TSK) filesystem interfaces. Expects an image handle, an APFS pool descriptor, a volume block identifier, and an optional password for decryption. Initializes internal TSK_FS_INFO structures for subsequent filesystem operations. Usage: create once per APFS volume to perform listing, walking, and metadata queries.
requirements: img_info must point to a valid, initialized TSK_IMG_INFO representing the underlying image
pool_info must point to a valid TSK_POOL_INFO describing the APFS pool that contains the target volume
vol_block must identify a valid APFS volume block number within the given pool (exact valid range unknown)
pass may be null-terminated C-string; empty string indicates no password or already unlocked (exact semantics unknown)
Object must remain alive for the duration of any operations using its fs_info or other member functions

functions.name: APFSFSCompat::fs_info
functions.description: Returns a const reference to the internal TSK_FS_INFO structure representing this APFS filesystem instance. Intended for read-only access to TSK filesystem metadata and callbacks.
requirements: Must be called on a properly constructed APFSFSCompat instance
Caller must not store the reference beyond the lifetime of the APFSFSCompat object
No exceptions are thrown (noexcept)

functions.name: APFSFSCompat::date_added
functions.signature: uint64_t date_added(uint64_t parent_id, uint64_t private_id) const noexcept
functions.description: Looks up the APFS 'date added' timestamp for an object identified by a private_id within a given parent directory (parent_id). Uses an internal cache for efficiency. Returns a 64-bit value representing the stored timestamp/epoch (exact epoch/units not specified).
requirements: parent_id must be a valid APFS directory identifier within this filesystem (exact range unknown)
private_id must be a valid item identifier within the given parent (exact range unknown)
No exceptions are thrown (noexcept)
If the object is not found, return value semantics are unknown (could be 0 or a sentinel)

functions.name: APFSFSCompat::file_add_meta
functions.description: Populates or augments the TSK_FS_FILE structure with metadata for the given inode number in this APFS filesystem. Typically invoked by TSK to load meta for files/directories.
requirements: The TSK_FS_FILE* must be non-null and point to an initialized TSK_FS_FILE
The TSK_INUM_T must reference a valid inode within this filesystem
No exceptions are thrown (noexcept)
Return value semantics (0/1 or TSK_OK/ERR) are not specified here; caller must consult implementation or TSK conventions

functions.name: APFSFSCompat::inode_walk
functions.signature: uint8_t inode_walk(TSK_FS_INFO* fs, TSK_INUM_T start_inum, TSK_INUM_T end_inum, TSK_FS_META_FLAG_ENUM flags, TSK_FS_META_WALK_CB action, void* ptr)
functions.description: Iterates over inodes in the range [start_inum, end_inum] and invokes the provided TSK metadata walk callback for each entry that matches the given flags. Integrates with TSK’s inode walking API.
requirements: fs must be non-null and reference the TSK_FS_INFO of this filesystem (or a compatible one)
start_inum and end_inum define an inclusive range; they must be within valid inode bounds (exact bounds unknown); start_inum should be <= end_inum
flags must be a valid combination of TSK_FS_META_FLAG_ENUM values as expected by TSK
action must be a valid function pointer conforming to TSK_FS_META_WALK_CB; it will be called for matching inodes
ptr is an opaque caller-supplied context passed to the callback; may be null
Return value semantics are not specified here; follow TSK conventions (unknown)

functions.name: APFSFSCompat::fsstat
functions.description: Writes filesystem statistics and summary information for this APFS volume to the given FILE stream (similar to TSK fsstat output).
requirements: FILE* must be a valid, writable stream (e.g., stdout, opened file)
Must be called on a properly constructed APFSFSCompat instance
No exceptions are thrown (noexcept)
Return value semantics are not specified here; follow TSK conventions (unknown)

functions.name: APFSFSCompat::load_attrs
functions.description: Loads and attaches extended attributes or resident attributes for the given TSK_FS_FILE from this APFS filesystem.
requirements: TSK_FS_FILE* must be non-null and initialized for a file object within this filesystem
No exceptions are thrown (noexcept)
Return value semantics are not specified here; follow TSK conventions (unknown)

functions.name: APFSFSCompat::istat
functions.signature: uint8_t istat(TSK_FS_ISTAT_FLAG_ENUM, FILE*, TSK_INUM_T, TSK_DADDR_T, int32_t) const noexcept
functions.description: Generates and writes detailed metadata (istat-style report) for a given inode to the provided FILE stream, honoring TSK istat flags. May accept an address and additional options per TSK semantics.
requirements: FILE* must be valid and writable
TSK_INUM_T must identify a valid inode within this filesystem
Flags must be valid TSK_FS_ISTAT_FLAG_ENUM values
No exceptions are thrown (noexcept)
Return value semantics are not specified here; follow TSK conventions (unknown)

functions.name: APFSFSCompat::block_walk
functions.signature: uint8_t block_walk(TSK_FS_INFO* , TSK_DADDR_T, TSK_DADDR_T, TSK_FS_BLOCK_WALK_FLAG_ENUM, TSK_FS_BLOCK_WALK_CB, void*)
functions.description: Walks blocks over the address range [start, end] according to TSK’s block walking interface, invoking the provided callback for each block that matches the given flags.
requirements: TSK_FS_INFO* must be non-null and correspond to this filesystem
The start and end TSK_DADDR_T parameters define an inclusive block address range; must be within valid bounds (exact bounds unknown); start should be <= end
Flags must be valid TSK_FS_BLOCK_WALK_FLAG_ENUM values
Callback must be a valid TSK_FS_BLOCK_WALK_CB pointer; it will be called for matching blocks
User context pointer may be null and is passed to the callback
Return value semantics are not specified here; follow TSK conventions (unknown)

functions.name: APFSFSCompat::block_getflags
functions.description: Returns TSK block flags for a given block address in this APFS filesystem (e.g., allocated/unallocated, metadata/data) according to TSK semantics.
requirements: TSK_FS_INFO* must be non-null and correspond to this filesystem
The TSK_DADDR_T must be a valid block address within the filesystem’s address space (exact bounds unknown)
Return value is a TSK_FS_BLOCK_FLAG_ENUM; specific flag meanings follow TSK definitions

functions.name: APFSFSCompat::decrypt_block
functions.description: Decrypts a single filesystem block identified by the given address into the provided buffer. Intended for APFS volumes with encryption enabled.
requirements: Block address (TSK_DADDR_T) must reference a readable block within this filesystem
The output buffer pointer must be non-null; required size and alignment are not specified here (unknown); caller must ensure it is large enough for one block
No exceptions are thrown (noexcept)
Return value semantics are not specified here; follow implementation or TSK conventions (unknown)

functions.name: APFSFSCompat::name_cmp
functions.signature: int name_cmp(const char*, const char*) const noexcept
functions.description: Compares two file or directory names according to APFS/TSK naming rules and returns an integer comparison result (exact ordering and case-sensitivity semantics unknown).
requirements: Both const char* arguments must be non-null, null-terminated C strings
No exceptions are thrown (noexcept)
Return value follows comparison convention (negative/zero/positive) is likely but not specified here (unknown)

functions.name: APFSFSCompat::dir_open_meta
functions.signature: TSK_RETVAL_ENUM dir_open_meta(TSK_FS_DIR**, TSK_INUM_T, int) const noexcept
functions.description: Opens a directory for reading by inode number and returns it via an output TSK_FS_DIR** according to TSK directory interface. The int parameter likely controls options or recursion (exact semantics unknown).
requirements: TSK_FS_DIR** must be non-null; on success, *out will point to a valid directory object managed per TSK rules
TSK_INUM_T must refer to a valid directory inode within this filesystem
The int options parameter must be set per TSK expectations (exact values unknown)
Must be called on a properly constructed APFSFSCompat instance
No exceptions are thrown (noexcept)
Return value is a TSK_RETVAL_ENUM indicating success/failure per TSK definitions

functions.name: tsk_apfs_fsstat
functions.description: Populates an apfs_fsstat_info structure with APFS filesystem statistics and metadata for the filesystem represented by fs_info. Typical usage is to query volume properties (name, UUID, role, capacity, times, etc.) after opening an APFS volume with The Sleuth Kit. Returns a status code (0 on success, non-zero on failure by common TSK convention).
requirements: fs_info must point to a valid, initialized TSK_FS_INFO for an APFS filesystem.
info must be non-null and point to writable memory for an apfs_fsstat_info structure.
Caller must check the return value and handle a non-zero result as an error.
The function only yields meaningful results for APFS volumes; passing a non-APFS fs_info will fail or return unspecified results (inferred from name and types).

functions.name: tsk_apfs_istat
functions.description: Retrieves APFS-specific file metadata for the given file handle and writes it to the provided apfs_istat_info structure (e.g., date_added, cloned inode number, BSD flags). Intended to be used after locating/opening a file within an APFS filesystem. Returns a status code (0 on success, non-zero on failure by common TSK convention).
requirements: fs_file must be a valid, initialized TSK_FS_FILE belonging to an APFS filesystem.
info must be non-null and point to writable memory for an apfs_istat_info structure.
Caller must check the return value and handle a non-zero result as an error.

functions.name: tsk_apfs_list_snapshots
functions.description: Enumerates APFS snapshots present in the filesystem referenced by fs_info and returns an allocated apfs_snapshot_list via list. The list contains a count (num_snapshots) and a flexible array of apfs_snapshot entries (name, XID, timestamp, dataless). The caller is responsible for freeing the returned list using tsk_apfs_free_snapshot_list. Returns a status code (0 on success, non-zero on failure by common TSK convention).
requirements: fs_info must point to a valid, initialized TSK_FS_INFO for an APFS filesystem.
list must be non-null and point to a variable capable of receiving the allocated apfs_snapshot_list pointer.
On success, the returned *list must be freed by calling tsk_apfs_free_snapshot_list; do not free it with standard free or other deallocators.
Caller must check the return value and handle a non-zero result as an error.
The returned structure uses a flexible array member (snapshots[0]); only access up to num_snapshots elements.

functions.name: tsk_apfs_free_snapshot_list
functions.description: Releases the memory associated with an apfs_snapshot_list previously returned by tsk_apfs_list_snapshots. Returns a status code (0 on success, non-zero on failure by common TSK convention).
requirements: list must be a pointer previously obtained from a successful call to tsk_apfs_list_snapshots.
After this call, the list pointer becomes invalid and must not be dereferenced.
Caller must check the return value and handle a non-zero result as an error.

functions.name: tsk_apfs_set_snapshot
functions.description: Sets the active APFS snapshot for the given filesystem handle to the snapshot identified by snap_xid (the snapshot’s transaction ID). Intended to scope subsequent filesystem operations (reads, listings, metadata queries) on fs_info to the specified snapshot. Returns a status code (0 on success, non-zero on failure by common TSK convention).
requirements: fs_info must point to a valid, initialized TSK_FS_INFO for an APFS filesystem.
snap_xid must correspond to a valid snapshot transaction ID present in the filesystem; otherwise the function fails.
Caller must check the return value and handle a non-zero result as an error.
Changing the active snapshot may affect all subsequent operations performed through fs_info (inferred from function name/purpose).

functions.name: APFSJObject::APFSJObject
functions.description: Default constructor. Creates an APFSJObject with default-initialized inode and empty collections. Result may be "invalid" until populated; use valid() to check.
requirements: Object is default-constructed; no parameters or side effects.
Callers should check valid() before assuming inode/extents are populated (inferred from presence of valid()).

functions.name: APFSJObject::APFSJObject
functions.description: Range-based constructor. Initializes an APFSJObject by scanning a pair of APFS journal object B-tree iterators [first, second) that describe records for a single object.
requirements: The iterators in the pair must be valid and form a half-open range [first, second) over APFSJObjBtreeNode.
Both iterators must refer to the same underlying container and be in a proper order (first reachable to second).
The records in the range should correspond to the same object ID for meaningful results (inferred from class purpose).

functions.name: APFSJObject::APFSJObject
functions.description: Iterator-pair constructor. Initializes an APFSJObject from a half-open range [first, second) over APFS journal object B-tree records.
requirements: 'first' and 'second' must be valid iterators into the same APFSJObjBtreeNode sequence.
Range must be well-formed: first must be reachable to second without undefined behavior.
Records in the range should belong to the same object ID for a coherent object (inferred from class purpose).

functions.name: APFSJObject::operator=
functions.description: Copy assignment operator. Replaces the contents of this APFSJObject with a copy of another.
requirements: Source object must be a valid APFSJObject instance.
After assignment, previously held resources in the target are overwritten (standard copy semantics).

functions.name: APFSJObject::operator=
functions.description: Move assignment operator. Transfers the contents of another APFSJObject into this one, leaving the source in a valid but unspecified state.
requirements: Source object may be in any state but will be left valid-yet-unspecified after move (standard move semantics).
Do not use moved-from object except to destroy, assign, or reinitialize (standard C++ guidance).

functions.name: APFSJObject::valid
functions.description: Returns true if the object represents a realized APFS journal object (inode.private_id != 0 or it has at least one extent).
requirements: No preconditions; callable on any APFSJObject instance.

functions.name: APFSJObject::child_count
functions.description: Returns the number of child directory entries associated with this object.
requirements: No preconditions; callable on any APFSJObject.

functions.name: APFSJObject::inode
functions.description: Returns a const reference to the underlying APFS inode structure for this object.
requirements: The returned reference remains valid as long as the APFSJObject is alive and not modified in a way that would reassign its inode.

functions.name: APFSJObject::name
functions.description: Returns the object name (e.g., filename) as a const reference.
requirements: The returned reference is valid while the APFSJObject remains alive.

functions.name: APFSJObject::extents
functions.description: Returns a const reference to the list of file extents (offset/physical/length/crypto_id) for this object.
requirements: The returned reference is valid while the APFSJObject remains alive.

functions.name: APFSJObject::inline_xattrs
functions.description: Returns a const reference to the inline extended attributes list (name/data pairs) for this object.
requirements: The returned reference is valid while the APFSJObject remains alive.

functions.name: APFSJObject::nonres_xattrs
functions.description: Returns a const reference to the non-resident extended attributes list (name/oid/size/allocated_size/crypto_id) for this object.
requirements: The returned reference is valid while the APFSJObject remains alive.

functions.name: APFSJObject::children
functions.description: Returns a const reference to the vector of child directory entries (name and directory record) for this object.
requirements: The returned reference is valid while the APFSJObject remains alive.

functions.name: APFSJObject::size
functions.description: Returns the logical file size (bytes) of the object.
requirements: No preconditions; callable on any APFSJObject.

functions.name: APFSJObject::size_on_disk
functions.description: Returns the allocated size on disk (bytes) for the object.
requirements: No preconditions; callable on any APFSJObject.

functions.name: APFSJObject::is_clone
functions.description: Indicates whether the object is a clone (APFS copy-on-write clone).
requirements: No preconditions; callable on any APFSJObject.

functions.name: APFSJObjTree::APFSJObjTree
functions.signature: APFSJObjTree::APFSJObjTree(const APFSPool &pool, apfs_block_num obj_omap, uint64_t root_tree_oid, const APFSFileSystem::crypto_info_t &crypto);
functions.description: Constructs an APFS journal object tree reader using a pool, object omap block number, the root tree object ID, and cryptographic information.
requirements: 'pool' must reference a valid APFS pool.
'obj_omap' must be a valid object map block number for the target volume.
'root_tree_oid' must be a valid object ID of the root tree to open.
'crypto' must contain the cryptographic parameters/keys required to access encrypted data if applicable.

functions.name: APFSJObjTree::APFSJObjTree
functions.description: Move constructor. Transfers ownership/state of an APFSJObjTree from another instance.
requirements: Source object will be left in a valid but unspecified state after move (standard move semantics).

functions.name: APFSJObjTree::obj
functions.description: Looks up and materializes an APFSJObject by object ID from the journal object tree. Returns a value object which can be checked with valid().
requirements: 'oid' should be an object ID present in the tree for a meaningful result; otherwise the returned APFSJObject may be invalid (check valid()).
The APFSJObjTree instance must have been successfully constructed (and optionally set to a snapshot) before calling.

functions.name: APFSJObjTree::set_snapshot
functions.description: Selects a snapshot (by transaction ID) to use for subsequent object enumeration/lookup.
requirements: 'snap_xid' must refer to a valid snapshot transaction ID in the underlying volume; behavior is unknown if not (not specified in header).
Must be called before begin()/obj() if a specific snapshot view is desired.

functions.name: APFSJObjTree::begin
functions.description: Returns an iterator to the first APFSJObject in the current tree/snapshot view.
requirements: The APFSJObjTree must be in a valid constructed state.
The returned iterator is valid until the APFSJObjTree is modified or destroyed.

functions.name: APFSJObjTree::end
functions.description: Returns a sentinel iterator representing the end of the APFSJObject sequence.
requirements: Use only for comparison; do not dereference the end iterator.

functions.name: APFSJObjTree::iterator::iterator
functions.description: Protected constructor. Creates an iterator bound to the given tree, positioned according to internal logic (likely begin/end).
requirements: 'tree' must be a valid, non-null pointer to an APFSJObjTree when constructing a usable iterator.
Noexcept: construction does not throw.

functions.name: APFSJObjTree::iterator::iterator
functions.description: Protected constructor. Creates an iterator bound to the given tree, positioned at or after the specified object ID.
requirements: 'tree' must be a valid, non-null pointer to an APFSJObjTree.
'oid' is an object ID used to initialize position; if not found, iterator may point to next greater or end (inferred from typical tree find_range behavior).

functions.name: APFSJObjTree::iterator::operator=
functions.description: Copy assignment operator for the iterator.
requirements: Both iterators must be from the same underlying tree for meaningful behavior (typical iterator requirement).

functions.name: APFSJObjTree::iterator::operator=
functions.description: Move assignment operator for the iterator.
requirements: After move, the source iterator is left in a valid but unspecified state; do not dereference it until reassigned.

functions.name: APFSJObjTree::iterator::operator*
functions.description: Dereference operator. Returns a const reference to the current APFSJObject the iterator points to.
requirements: The iterator must not be equal to end(); dereferencing end is undefined.
Underlying APFSJObjTree must outlive the iterator to keep references valid.

functions.name: APFSJObjTree::iterator::operator->
functions.description: Member-access operator. Returns a pointer to the current APFSJObject.
requirements: The iterator must not be equal to end(); using operator-> on end is undefined.
The returned pointer remains valid as long as the iterator remains valid and not advanced past the element.

functions.name: APFSJObjTree::iterator::operator++
functions.description: Prefix increment. Advances the iterator to the next APFSJObject and returns a reference to the iterator.
requirements: The iterator must be dereferenceable prior to increment; incrementing past end results in an end iterator.
Do not increment an end iterator (undefined behavior by convention).

functions.name: APFSJObjTree::iterator::operator++
functions.description: Postfix increment. Advances the iterator to the next APFSJObject and returns a copy of the prior APFSJObject value.
requirements: The iterator must be dereferenceable prior to increment; do not call on an end iterator.

functions.name: APFSJObjTree::iterator::operator==
functions.description: Equality comparison. Iterators are equal if they refer to the same tree and have the same next-position state.
requirements: Both iterators must be comparable; comparing iterators from different trees is allowed here but only returns true if both tree pointers and positions match.

functions.name: APFSJObjTree::iterator::operator!=
functions.description: Inequality comparison, logical negation of operator==.
requirements: Same requirements as operator==.

functions.name: zlib_inflate
functions.signature: extern int zlib_inflate(char* source, uint64_t sourceLen, char* dest, uint64_t destLen, uint64_t* uncompressedLength, unsigned long* bytesConsumed);
functions.description: Decompresses a zlib-compressed byte stream from source into dest. Intended for use by APFS/HFS+ decmpfs handlers to expand in-attribute or resource-fork zlib data. On success, writes the number of decompressed bytes to uncompressedLength and the number of input bytes consumed to bytesConsumed.
requirements: source must point to a readable buffer of at least sourceLen bytes.
dest must point to a writable buffer of at least destLen bytes.
uncompressedLength must be a valid, writable pointer if the caller expects the decompressed byte count to be returned.
bytesConsumed must be a valid, writable pointer if the caller expects the number of input bytes consumed to be returned.
source must contain data in zlib format; behavior is undefined for other formats.
destLen must be large enough to hold the uncompressed data; truncation behavior is unknown from this header and should be avoided by providing a sufficiently large buffer.

functions.name: decmpfs_file_read_zlib_attr
functions.signature: extern int decmpfs_file_read_zlib_attr(TSK_FS_FILE* fs_file, char* buffer, TSK_OFF_T attributeLength, uint64_t uncSize);
functions.description: Reads and decompresses a zlib-compressed APFS/HFS+ decmpfs attribute (in-line attribute form) from the given file into buffer. Use when compression_type indicates zlib data stored directly within the com.apple.decmpfs xattr.
requirements: fs_file must be a valid, initialized TSK_FS_FILE for a file that has a com.apple.decmpfs attribute containing zlib-compressed data (DECMPFS_TYPE_ZLIB_ATTR).
buffer must point to a writable memory region large enough to hold the uncompressed data (at least uncSize bytes).

attributeLength should be the length in bytes of the decmpfs attribute value that contains the compressed payload (excluding the on-disk decmpfs header, if required by the implementation; exact expectations are not specified here).
uncSize must be the expected uncompressed size (as indicated by the decmpfs header).
Function returns an int status (exact conventions not documented here); callers should check for non-zero/negative values as error indicators per TSK conventions.

functions.description: Reads and decompresses an LZVN-compressed APFS/HFS+ decmpfs attribute (in-line attribute form) from the given file into buffer. Use when compression_type indicates LZVN data stored directly within the com.apple.decmpfs xattr.
requirements: fs_file must be a valid, initialized TSK_FS_FILE for a file that has a com.apple.decmpfs attribute containing LZVN-compressed data (DECMPFS_TYPE_LZVN_ATTR).
buffer must point to a writable memory region large enough to hold the uncompressed data (at least uncSize bytes).

attributeLength should be the length in bytes of the decmpfs attribute value that contains the compressed payload (excluding the on-disk decmpfs header, if required by the implementation; exact expectations are not specified here).

Function returns an int status (exact conventions not documented here); callers should check for non-zero/negative values as error indicators per TSK conventions.

functions.name: decmpfs_attr_walk_zlib_rsrc
functions.signature: extern uint8_t decmpfs_attr_walk_zlib_rsrc(const TSK_FS_ATTR * fs_attr, int flags, TSK_FS_FILE_WALK_CB a_action, void *ptr);
functions.description: Iterates (walks) the data of a zlib-compressed decmpfs resource-fork stream, invoking the provided callback for data chunks. Intended for files where compressed data is stored in the resource fork (DECMPFS_TYPE_ZLIB_RSRC).
requirements: fs_attr must be a valid pointer to a TSK_FS_ATTR that represents the file's resource-fork attribute containing the CMPF resource for zlib compression.
a_action must be a valid callback of type TSK_FS_FILE_WALK_CB; it will be invoked per walked chunk. The callback must adhere to TSK’s expected semantics for returning control and error status.
ptr is an opaque user pointer passed to the callback; may be NULL if unused.
flags controls the walk behavior (e.g., which ranges to visit); specific flag meanings are defined by TSK and must be chosen accordingly (not specified in this header).
The function returns a uint8_t status per TSK walk conventions; callers must check the return code for success/failure per TSK documentation.

functions.name: decmpfs_attr_walk_lzvn_rsrc
functions.signature: extern uint8_t decmpfs_attr_walk_lzvn_rsrc(const TSK_FS_ATTR * fs_attr, int flags, TSK_FS_FILE_WALK_CB a_action, void *ptr);
functions.description: Iterates (walks) the data of an LZVN-compressed decmpfs resource-fork stream, invoking the provided callback for data chunks. Intended for files where compressed data is stored in the resource fork (DECMPFS_TYPE_LZVN_RSRC).
requirements: fs_attr must be a valid pointer to a TSK_FS_ATTR that represents the file's resource-fork attribute containing the CMPF resource for LZVN compression.
a_action must be a valid callback of type TSK_FS_FILE_WALK_CB; it will be invoked per walked chunk. The callback must adhere to TSK’s expected semantics for returning control and error status.
ptr is an opaque user pointer passed to the callback; may be NULL if unused.
flags controls the walk behavior (e.g., which ranges to visit); specific flag meanings are defined by TSK and must be chosen accordingly (not specified in this header).
The function returns a uint8_t status per TSK walk conventions; callers must check the return code for success/failure per TSK documentation.

functions.name: decmpfs_file_read_zlib_rsrc
functions.signature: extern ssize_t decmpfs_file_read_zlib_rsrc(const TSK_FS_ATTR * a_fs_attr, TSK_OFF_T a_offset, char *a_buf, size_t a_len);
functions.description: Reads bytes from a file whose content is stored in a zlib-compressed decmpfs resource fork, returning decompressed data into a_buf starting at the specified logical offset. Suitable for random-access reads of the decompressed content (compression units are typically 64 KiB).
requirements: a_fs_attr must be a valid TSK_FS_ATTR referencing the resource-fork attribute that holds the CMPF zlib-compressed data table/stream.
a_buf must point to a writable buffer of at least a_len bytes.

a_offset is the logical byte offset in the uncompressed stream to begin reading; it should be within the file’s uncompressed size. Behavior for out-of-range offsets is not specified here and should be avoided.
a_len is the maximum number of bytes to read; the function returns the number of bytes actually read (ssize_t).
Callers must check the return value: negative values typically indicate an error per TSK conventions; zero may indicate EOF.

functions.name: decmpfs_file_read_lzvn_rsrc

functions.name: handleVolumeEncryption
functions.signature: int handleVolumeEncryption(TSK_FS_INFO* a_fs_info, const char* a_pass);
functions.description: Initialize and/or unlock volume-level encryption for the filesystem referenced by a_fs_info using the supplied passphrase a_pass. Intended to be called before reading encrypted content so that decryption metadata/keys are prepared and attached to a_fs_info. Exact return-value semantics are not documented in this header; success/failure conventions are unknown.
requirements: a_fs_info must be a valid, initialized pointer to a TSK_FS_INFO associated with the target volume/filesystem.
a_pass should be a valid, null-terminated C string containing the passphrase or credential; whether NULL is allowed is unknown.
Must be called before attempting reads that require decryption (inferred from purpose).
Caller must handle the function’s int return code; exact success/error values are unknown and should be checked against the library’s documentation or source.
Thread-safety is unknown; avoid concurrent calls on the same a_fs_info unless documented safe.

functions.name: tsk_fs_get_encryption_description
functions.signature: void tsk_fs_get_encryption_description(TSK_FS_INFO* a_fs_info, char* a_desc, size_t a_descLen);
functions.description: Retrieve a human-readable description of the encryption state/algorithm(s) for the filesystem represented by a_fs_info and write it into the caller-provided buffer a_desc up to a_descLen bytes. Use to present or log the encryption status. Behavior regarding NUL-termination and truncation is not specified here.
requirements: a_fs_info must be a valid, initialized pointer to the relevant TSK_FS_INFO.
a_desc must point to a writable buffer of at least a_descLen bytes.
a_descLen should accurately reflect the size of a_desc; if 0, nothing can be written (termination behavior is unknown).
Call only after any required encryption handling/initialization (e.g., after handleVolumeEncryption) to get an up-to-date description (inferred).
Assume the function will not write more than a_descLen bytes; NUL-termination on truncation is unknown.

functions.name: read_and_decrypt_bitlocker_blocks
functions.signature: ssize_t read_and_decrypt_bitlocker_blocks(TSK_FS_INFO* a_fs_info, TSK_DADDR_T start, size_t len, void* data);
functions.description: Read and decrypt data from a BitLocker-encrypted volume starting at block/address start for len bytes and store the result in the buffer data. Returns the number of bytes read on success or a negative value on error (typical ssize_t convention; exact semantics not guaranteed by this header). Only available when compiled with HAVE_LIBMBEDTLS defined, and requires that the volume’s decryption context has been initialized/unlocked beforehand.
requirements: Available only if the library is built with HAVE_LIBMBEDTLS defined.
a_fs_info must be valid and must reference a BitLocker-encrypted volume with decryption metadata/keys already initialized (e.g., via handleVolumeEncryption).
start must be within the addressable range of the underlying volume; units are inferred to be logical block/sector address based on TSK_DADDR_T naming (exact unit size unknown).
len must be the number of bytes to read/decrypt; it should be nonzero and small enough that data has capacity for at least len bytes.
data must point to a writable buffer with capacity >= len bytes.
Caller must check the ssize_t return value for errors and partial reads; negative indicates error by convention (exact error model unknown).
Thread-safety and reentrancy are unknown; avoid concurrent operations on the same a_fs_info unless documented safe.

functions.name: freeEncryptionData
functions.description: Release and clean up any encryption-related metadata, keys, or state associated with a_fs_info. Call during teardown to prevent leaks and to detach encryption state from the filesystem context. After this call, decryption-dependent operations may fail until re-initialized.
requirements: a_fs_info must be a valid TSK_FS_INFO pointer that may have encryption data attached.
Should be called when encryption handling is no longer needed for a_fs_info (e.g., before destroying or reusing the structure).
Do not use encryption-dependent operations on a_fs_info after calling this function unless reinitialized (inferred).
It is unknown whether multiple calls are safe; avoid double-free by calling at most once per initialization unless the implementation documents idempotence.
Thread-safety is unknown; avoid concurrent calls with other operations on the same a_fs_info.

functions.name: APFSBtreeNodeIterator::APFSBtreeNodeIterator
functions.description: Default-constructs an invalid/end iterator for a B-tree node. Conforms to ForwardIterator requirements (DefaultConstructible).
requirements: Resulting iterator is not associated with any node until assigned or constructed with a node.

functions.name: APFSBtreeNodeIterator::operator=
functions.description: Copy-assigns this iterator from rhs, duplicating node, index, and child/value state.
requirements: Self-assignment is handled.
rhs may be end or valid; copying end is allowed.

functions.name: APFSBtreeNodeIterator::operator++
functions.description: Pre-increment: advances the iterator to the next entry. On leaf nodes, increments index and refreshes value; on internal nodes, advances child iterator and climbs to the next key when needed.
requirements: Iterator should not be incremented past end repeatedly; doing so keeps it at end.
May reconstruct internal state; can throw runtime_error indirectly via reinitialization when validating offsets.

functions.name: APFSBtreeNodeIterator::operator++
functions.description: Post-increment: returns a copy of the current iterator state, then advances this iterator using pre-increment.
requirements: Same requirements as pre-increment. Returned iterator is a previous position snapshot.

functions.name: APFSBtreeNodeIterator::operator==
functions.description: Compares two iterators for equality. Iterators are equal if they reference the same node and index and, for internal nodes, their child iterators compare equal.
requirements: Iterators must be comparable even if one or both are end. Both null nodes compare equal.

functions.name: APFSBtreeNodeIterator::operator!=
functions.description: Negation of operator==.
requirements: Same as operator==.

functions.name: APFSBtreeNodeIterator::is_valid
functions.description: Returns true if the iterator references a node and the index is within the key range of that node.
requirements: None; safe to call on default-constructed or end iterators.

functions.name: APFSBtreeNodeIterator::operator*
functions.description: Dereferences the iterator to the current key/value pair. For internal nodes, defers to the current child iterator’s dereference.
requirements: If the iterator is at end (index >= key_count()), dereferencing returns the last cached value for leaves or the underlying child’s value for internal nodes; callers should check is_valid() or compare with end() before dereferencing to avoid undefined access patterns.

functions.name: APFSBtreeNodeIterator::operator->
functions.description: Pointer dereference to the current key/value pair. For internal nodes, defers to the child iterator’s pointer.
requirements: As with operator*, callers should ensure iterator is not at end before use.

functions.name: APFSBtreeNode::end

Caller should check return value to confirm unlocked state.

functions.name: APFSFileSystem::uuid
functions.description: Returns the volume UUID.
requirements: Volume superblock must be valid.

functions.name: APFSFileSystem::name
functions.description: Returns the volume name as a string.
requirements: Volume superblock must be valid; encoding is presumed UTF-8 or UTF-16-to-UTF-8 converted elsewhere (unknown).

functions.name: APFSFileSystem::formatted_by
functions.description: Returns the string identifying the tool/version that formatted the volume.
requirements: Volume superblock must be valid.

functions.name: APFSFileSystem::password_hint
functions.description: Returns the password hint string stored in the volume’s crypto metadata.
requirements: Crypto info must be initialized; empty string if none.

functions.name: APFSFileSystem::crypto_info
functions.description: Returns a const reference to the structure holding detailed crypto state (wrapped VEK/KEKs, flags, passwords, etc.).
requirements: Structure lifetime tied to APFSFileSystem; reference remains valid as long as the filesystem object exists.

functions.name: APFSFileSystem::decryption_key
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the plaintext volume encryption key (VEK) if the filesystem is unlocked; otherwise returns nullptr.
requirements: Call unlock() or construct with a password to populate the VEK.
Pointer remains valid while the filesystem object remains alive and unlocked.

functions.name: APFSFileSystem::role
functions.description: Returns the APFS volume role (e.g., system, data) from the superblock.
requirements: Volume superblock must be valid.

functions.name: APFSFileSystem::reserved
functions.description: Returns the reserved space in bytes (reserve_blocks * block_size).
requirements: Volume superblock must be valid.

functions.name: APFSFileSystem::quota
functions.description: Returns the quota in bytes (quota_blocks * block_size).
requirements: Volume superblock must be valid.

functions.name: APFSFileSystem::used
functions.description: Returns the used space in bytes (alloc_blocks * block_size).
requirements: Volume superblock must be valid.

functions.name: APFSFileSystem::reserved_blocks
functions.description: Returns the number of reserved blocks.
requirements: Volume superblock must be valid.

functions.name: APFSFileSystem::quota_blocks
functions.description: Returns the number of quota blocks.
requirements: Volume superblock must be valid.

functions.name: APFSFileSystem::alloc_blocks
functions.description: Returns the number of allocated blocks.
requirements: Volume superblock must be valid.

functions.name: APFSFileSystem::last_inum
functions.description: Returns the last assigned inode number (next_inum - 1).
requirements: Volume superblock must be valid.

functions.name: APFSFileSystem::encrypted
functions.description: Returns true if the volume is encrypted (i.e., APFS_SB_UNENCRYPTED flag is not set).
requirements: Volume superblock must be valid.

functions.name: APFSFileSystem::case_sensitive
functions.description: Returns true if the volume is case-sensitive (i.e., APFS_SB_INCOMPAT_CASE_INSENSITIVE flag is not set).
requirements: Volume superblock must be valid.

functions.name: APFSFileSystem::created
functions.description: Returns the creation timestamp of the volume (APFS epoch).
requirements: Volume superblock must be valid.

functions.name: APFSFileSystem::changed
functions.description: Returns the last modification timestamp of the volume (APFS epoch).
requirements: Volume superblock must be valid.

functions.name: APFSFileSystem::unmount_log
functions.description: Returns the unmount log entries, including timestamps, messages, and last XID values.
requirements: Metadata containing the unmount log must be present and readable; may throw if corrupted.

functions.name: APFSFileSystem::omap_root
functions.description: Returns the block number of the filesystem’s OMAP root.
requirements: Filesystem metadata must be readable; may throw if invalid.

functions.name: APFSFileSystem::root_jobj_tree
functions.description: Builds and returns the root JObj tree for the filesystem, used to locate file system objects.
requirements: APFSJObjTree must be constructible from available metadata; may throw if prerequisites (object tree, keys) are missing.

functions.name: APFSFileSystem::extent_ref_tree
functions.description: Returns the root node of the extent reference B-tree for this filesystem.
requirements: fs()->extentref_tree_oid must reference a valid node; construction may throw if invalid.

functions.name: APFSFileSystem::snap_meta_tree
functions.description: Returns the root node of the snapshot metadata B-tree for this filesystem.
requirements: fs()->snap_meta_tree_oid must reference a valid node; construction may throw if invalid.

functions.name: APFSJObjKey::oid
functions.description: Extracts and returns the 60-bit object ID from oid_and_type.
requirements: oid_and_type must be populated correctly.

functions.name: APFSJObjKey::type
functions.description: Extracts and returns the 4-bit type field from oid_and_type.
requirements: oid_and_type must be populated correctly.

functions.name: btrfs_csum_crc32c
functions.signature: unsigned long btrfs_csum_crc32c(const unsigned char *a_data, const int a_len);
functions.description: Computes a CRC32C (Castagnoli) checksum over a_data buffer of length a_len bytes. Intended for validating Btrfs structures that use CRC32C. Returns the checksum value; exact width is not documented here, but CRC32C is a 32-bit value typically returned in the lower 32 bits of unsigned long. Behavior for a_len == 0 is expected to be the CRC of an empty buffer (inferred); no error reporting is specified.
requirements: a_data must be a valid pointer to at least a_len readable bytes when a_len > 0.
a_len must be >= 0 (length is a count of bytes).
If a_len == 0, a_data may be NULL or any value will not be dereferenced (behavior inferred; not explicitly documented).
The function performs no allocation and has no side effects; caller is responsible for any higher-level error handling as no error code is returned (inferred from signature).

functions.name: exfatfs_open
functions.description: Initializes exFAT-specific state in a FATFS_INFO structure for use by Sleuth Kit exFAT processing. Likely verifies on-disk exFAT structures and populates derived fields needed by other helpers. Returns a status byte (0/1 convention is unknown).
requirements: a_fatfs must be a valid, writable pointer to an initialized FATFS_INFO associated with an exFAT volume.
The underlying image/device referenced by a_fatfs must be accessible for reading.
Return-value convention is not documented; callers must consult implementation or broader TSK conventions to interpret non-zero/zero status.
Thread-safety and reentrancy are unknown.

functions.name: exfatfs_is_cluster_alloc
functions.description: Determines whether the specified exFAT cluster is allocated according to the allocation bitmap/FAT metadata. Returns an int8_t status indicating allocated/free/unknown (exact mapping is not documented).
requirements: a_fatfs must be a valid pointer to a mounted/initialized exFAT FATFS_INFO (e.g., after exfatfs_open).
a_cluster_addr must refer to a valid cluster number within the cluster heap (>= EXFATFS_FIRST_CLUSTER).
The function may consult allocation bitmap or FAT; the relevant tables must be readable via a_fatfs.
Exact return semantics are not documented; callers should handle potential tri-state (-1/0/1) patterns common in TSK.

functions.name: exfatfs_fsstat
functions.description: Emits filesystem statistics for an exFAT volume to the provided FILE stream (e.g., fsstat output). Uses TSK_FS_INFO to read metadata and formats details for exFAT.
requirements: a_fs must be a valid, initialized TSK_FS_INFO for an exFAT filesystem.
a_hFile must be a valid writable FILE* (e.g., stdout, a file opened for writing).
The underlying image/device must be readable.
Return semantics (success/failure) are not documented.

functions.name: exfatfs_is_dentry
functions.signature: extern uint8_t exfatfs_is_dentry(FATFS_INFO *a_fatfs, FATFS_DENTRY *a_dentry, FATFS_DATA_UNIT_ALLOC_STATUS_ENUM a_cluster_is_alloc, uint8_t a_do_basic_tests_only);
functions.description: Validates whether the given on-disk 32-byte entry buffer represents any known exFAT directory entry type and optionally performs only basic structural tests. Uses allocation status context for additional checks.
requirements: a_fatfs must be a valid pointer to exFAT FATFS_INFO (structure/layout information required).
a_dentry must point to a readable FATFS_DENTRY buffer holding a raw directory entry from disk.
a_cluster_is_alloc must reflect the allocation state of the containing cluster; value must be a member of FATFS_DATA_UNIT_ALLOC_STATUS_ENUM.
a_do_basic_tests_only controls depth of validation; accepted values are 0/1 (other values unspecified).
Returns a byte flag; precise success convention is not documented.

functions.name: exfatfs_is_vol_label_dentry
functions.description: Checks whether the given directory entry is an exFAT Volume Label entry (type 0x03 with allocation bit semantics).
requirements: a_dentry must point to a valid FATFS_DENTRY read from disk.
a_cluster_is_alloc must be a valid FATFS_DATA_UNIT_ALLOC_STATUS_ENUM reflecting the containing cluster's allocation.
Only root-directory entries should be volume label entries per exFAT; caller context should ensure the entry is from the root directory if enforcing placement.

functions.name: exfatfs_is_vol_guid_dentry
functions.description: Determines whether a directory entry is an exFAT Volume GUID entry (type 0x20 with allocation status in high bit).
requirements: a_dentry must be a readable FATFS_DENTRY pointer.
a_alloc_status must be a valid FATFS_DATA_UNIT_ALLOC_STATUS_ENUM value for the entry's cluster.
Volume GUID entries are expected only in the root directory; caller should ensure proper directory context if required.

functions.name: exfatfs_is_alloc_bitmap_dentry
functions.description: Tests whether a directory entry describes an exFAT Allocation Bitmap (type 0x01 with flags distinguishing primary/secondary). May use FATFS_INFO for bounds validation.
requirements: a_dentry must point to a valid FATFS_DENTRY buffer.
a_alloc_status must be set according to the entry’s cluster allocation state.
a_fatfs must be a valid exFAT FATFS_INFO to verify cluster and length constraints.
Allocation bitmap entries should appear only in the root directory; placement enforcement is caller-dependent.

functions.name: exfatfs_is_upcase_table_dentry
functions.description: Checks whether the entry is an exFAT Upcase Table directory entry (type 0x02) and optionally validates sizes/locations using filesystem context.
requirements: a_dentry must point to a valid on-disk directory entry.
a_alloc_status must indicate allocation status for the containing cluster.
a_fatfs must be a valid exFAT FATFS_INFO for additional structural checks.
Upcase table entries are expected only in the root directory.

functions.name: exfatfs_is_texfat_dentry
functions.description: Identifies a TexFAT (transactional exFAT) directory entry (type 0x21).
requirements: a_dentry must be a valid FATFS_DENTRY pointer.
a_alloc_status must be a valid FATFS_DATA_UNIT_ALLOC_STATUS_ENUM.
TexFAT entries appear in the root directory; caller context should reflect that if enforcing placement.

functions.name: exfatfs_is_access_ctrl_table_dentry
functions.description: Determines whether a directory entry is an exFAT Access Control Table entry (type 0x62).
requirements: a_dentry must be a readable FATFS_DENTRY pointer.
a_alloc_status must be a valid FATFS_DATA_UNIT_ALLOC_STATUS_ENUM.
Access control table entries are expected only in the root directory.

functions.name: exfatfs_is_file_dentry
functions.description: Checks if a directory entry is a primary File directory entry (type 0x05/0x85) in exFAT and may validate secondary count ranges. Uses filesystem context for endian/layout.
requirements: a_dentry must point to a valid FATFS_DENTRY.
a_fatfs must be a valid exFAT FATFS_INFO, including correct endianness and volume parameters.
File primary entries should report 2–18 secondary entries; enforcement specifics are internal.

functions.name: exfatfs_is_file_dentry_standalone
functions.description: Standalone validator for a File primary directory entry without needing a full FATFS_INFO. Uses the provided endianness for field interpretation.
requirements: a_dentry must be a valid pointer to a directory entry buffer.
a_endian must be a valid TSK_ENDIAN_ENUM matching the on-disk entry's endianness (exFAT uses little-endian).

functions.name: exfatfs_is_file_stream_dentry
functions.description: Checks whether an entry is a File Stream extension entry (type 0x40/0xC0) and validates internal invariants using filesystem context (lengths, flags, cluster bounds).
requirements: a_dentry must point to a valid FATFS_DENTRY containing a stream extension entry.
a_fatfs must be a valid exFAT FATFS_INFO providing cluster heap size and last-cluster information.

functions.name: exfatfs_is_file_stream_dentry_standalone
functions.signature: extern uint8_t exfatfs_is_file_stream_dentry_standalone(FATFS_DENTRY *a_dentry, TSK_ENDIAN_ENUM a_endian, uint64_t a_cluster_heap_size, TSK_DADDR_T a_last_cluster);
functions.description: Standalone validator for an exFAT File Stream directory entry using only endianness and basic volume bounds (cluster heap size and last cluster), without full FATFS_INFO.
requirements: a_dentry must be a valid pointer to a raw directory entry buffer.
a_endian must be a valid TSK_ENDIAN_ENUM (exFAT is little-endian; mismatched values may cause misinterpretation).
a_cluster_heap_size must be the count of clusters in the heap (>= 0) and consistent with the volume.
a_last_cluster must be a valid cluster index bound consistent with a_cluster_heap_size.

functions.name: exfatfs_find_file_stream_dentry
functions.signature: extern uint8_t exfatfs_find_file_stream_dentry(FATFS_INFO *a_fatfs, TSK_INUM_T a_file_entry_inum, TSK_DADDR_T a_sector, uint8_t a_sector_is_alloc, EXFATFS_DIR_ENTRY_TYPE a_file_dentry_type, FATFS_DENTRY *a_stream_dentry);
functions.description: Given a primary File directory entry (by inode/offset context), locates the corresponding File Stream extension entry in the directory stream and copies it into a_stream_dentry. Uses sector location and allocation context to guide search/validation.
requirements: a_fatfs must be a valid exFAT FATFS_INFO providing directory reading capability.
a_file_entry_inum must identify the target file entry; valid range per filesystem.
a_sector must be the sector address where the file entry resides or where scanning should begin; must be valid for the volume.
a_sector_is_alloc should indicate allocation status of the sector (0/1 expected).
a_file_dentry_type must be a valid EXFATFS_DIR_ENTRY_TYPE corresponding to a file primary entry (0x05/0x85).
a_stream_dentry must be a valid, writable pointer where the found stream entry will be stored.

functions.name: exfatfs_is_file_name_dentry
functions.description: Determines whether an entry is an exFAT File Name directory entry (type 0x41/0xC1).
requirements: a_dentry must be a valid pointer to a directory entry buffer read from disk.

functions.name: exfatfs_dinode_copy
functions.signature: extern TSK_RETVAL_ENUM exfatfs_dinode_copy(FATFS_INFO *a_fatfs, TSK_INUM_T a_inum, FATFS_DENTRY *a_dentry, uint8_t a_is_alloc, TSK_FS_FILE *a_fs_file);
functions.description: Builds and copies inode metadata for an exFAT directory entry into a TSK_FS_FILE structure. Uses the raw dentry, its allocation state, and filesystem context to populate attributes and data runs.
requirements: a_fatfs must be a valid exFAT FATFS_INFO with readable volume data.
a_inum must refer to the target file’s inode number within range for the filesystem.
a_dentry must point to the corresponding on-disk directory entry for the inode.
a_is_alloc indicates whether the dentry is allocated (0/1 expected).
a_fs_file must be a valid, writable TSK_FS_FILE to receive populated metadata.
Caller must check the returned TSK_RETVAL_ENUM for success/failure per TSK conventions.

functions.name: exfatfs_inode_lookup
functions.signature: extern uint8_t exfatfs_inode_lookup(FATFS_INFO *a_fatfs, TSK_FS_FILE *a_fs_file, TSK_INUM_T a_inum);
functions.description: Looks up an exFAT inode by number and populates a provided TSK_FS_FILE with its metadata and attributes.
requirements: a_fatfs must be a valid exFAT FATFS_INFO.
a_fs_file must be a valid, writable TSK_FS_FILE pointer.
a_inum must be a valid inode number for the volume (within allocated range).
Return semantics (0/1) are not documented; caller should consult TSK usage patterns.

functions.name: exfatfs_istat_attr_flags
functions.signature: extern uint8_t exfatfs_istat_attr_flags(FATFS_INFO *a_fatfs, TSK_INUM_T a_inum, FILE *a_hFile);
functions.description: Prints or reports exFAT attribute flags for the specified inode to the provided FILE stream (for istat-style output).
requirements: a_fatfs must be a valid exFAT FATFS_INFO.
a_inum must be a valid inode number.
a_hFile must be a valid writable FILE*.
Return value meaning is not documented.

functions.name: exfatfs_inode_walk_should_skip_dentry
functions.signature: extern uint8_t exfatfs_inode_walk_should_skip_dentry(FATFS_INFO *a_fatfs, TSK_INUM_T a_inum, FATFS_DENTRY *a_dentry, unsigned int a_selection_flags, int a_cluster_is_alloc);
functions.description: Determines, during an inode/directory walk, whether a given directory entry should be skipped based on selection flags, inode context, and allocation status.
requirements: a_fatfs must be a valid exFAT FATFS_INFO.
a_inum must be the inode number associated with the directory being walked or entry context.
a_dentry must be a valid FATFS_DENTRY pointer.
a_selection_flags must be a valid bitmask according to the caller’s walk criteria (exact bits not documented).
a_cluster_is_alloc must indicate allocation status for the containing cluster; expected to be boolean-like.

functions.name: exfatfs_get_alloc_status_from_type
functions.description: Extracts the allocation status from an exFAT directory entry type byte (high bit indicates allocation). Returns a normalized status byte.
requirements: a_dir_entry_type must be a raw exFAT directory entry type byte read from disk.
The function interprets only allocation bit; caller must handle type classification separately if needed.

functions.name: exfatfs_get_enum_from_type
functions.description: Maps a raw exFAT directory entry type byte to its enumerated type with the allocation bit masked off (e.g., 0xC1 -> FILE_NAME).
requirements: a_dir_entry_type must be a raw directory entry type byte from disk.
Caller must not pass arbitrary values outside 0x00–0xFF; behavior for unknown types is not documented.

functions.name: exfatfs_dent_parse_buf
functions.signature: extern TSK_RETVAL_ENUM exfatfs_dent_parse_buf(FATFS_INFO *a_fatfs, TSK_FS_DIR *a_fs_dir, char *a_buf, TSK_OFF_T a_buf_len, TSK_DADDR_T *a_sector_addrs, int recursion_depth);
functions.description: Parses a buffer containing exFAT directory entries into a TSK_FS_DIR structure, using filesystem context to interpret entries. May recurse into subdirectories up to a specified depth. Sector address array correlates entries to disk locations.
requirements: a_fatfs must be a valid exFAT FATFS_INFO for reading and interpreting entries.
a_fs_dir must be a valid, writable TSK_FS_DIR to receive parsed entries.
a_buf must point to a readable memory buffer containing raw directory entry bytes; must be at least a_buf_len bytes.
a_buf_len must be non-negative and a multiple of the on-disk entry size (32 bytes) for complete parsing; behavior on non-multiples is unspecified.
a_sector_addrs must be a valid pointer to an array mapping buffer segments to sector addresses; required size/layout are implementation-specific and not documented here.
recursion_depth must be within caller-defined safety limits to avoid unbounded recursion; exact maximum is not documented.
Caller must check the returned TSK_RETVAL_ENUM for success/failure.

functions.name: ext2fs_dir_open_meta
functions.signature: TSK_RETVAL_ENUM ext2fs_dir_open_meta(TSK_FS_INFO * a_fs, TSK_FS_DIR ** a_fs_dir, TSK_INUM_T a_addr, int recursion_depth);
functions.description: Open a directory by inode number (metadata address) in an EXT2/EXT3/EXT4 filesystem and return a populated TSK_FS_DIR handle. Typical usage is to pass an initialized TSK_FS_INFO for an EXT* image, an output location for the directory handle, and the target directory inode. The recursion_depth parameter is used by the library to limit internal recursion when processing nested structures (exact semantics not documented here). Returns a TSK_RETVAL_ENUM status code indicating success or failure. Details such as whether non-directory inodes are allowed or how errors are signaled beyond the return value are not documented in this header.
requirements: a_fs must be a non-NULL pointer to an initialized filesystem handle compatible with EXT2/EXT3/EXT4 (typically an EXT2FS_INFO embedded in TSK_FS_INFO).
a_fs_dir must be non-NULL and point to a variable where the function can store the resulting TSK_FS_DIR pointer.
a_addr should be a valid inode number in the filesystem; if it does not identify a directory, the call may fail (inferred from function name and common TSK patterns).
Caller must check the returned TSK_RETVAL_ENUM and handle errors accordingly; specific error codes are not documented here.
Ownership/lifetime of the returned TSK_FS_DIR is managed by the caller per TSK conventions (exact free/close routine not specified here; consult TSK API).
recursion_depth usage and valid range are not documented in this header; callers should treat it as library-defined and avoid extreme values (unknown exact constraints).

functions.name: ext2fs_jentry_walk
functions.signature: uint8_t ext2fs_jentry_walk(TSK_FS_INFO * a_fs, int flags, TSK_FS_JENTRY_WALK_CB cb, void *cb_ctx);
functions.description: Iterate over journal entries for an EXT* filesystem and invoke a callback for each entry encountered. Intended for analyzing the ext3/4 JBD/JBD2 journal at the logical journal-entry level. The flags parameter controls walk behavior (filtering, ordering, etc.), cb is invoked per entry, and cb_ctx is user context passed to the callback. Returns a status byte (success/failure semantics not documented here).
requirements: a_fs must be a non-NULL pointer to an initialized EXT* filesystem handle with journal access available.
cb must be non-NULL; the function will call it for each journal entry found.
cb_ctx may be NULL or any user-supplied context pointer (not further specified here).
flags meaning and valid combinations are not documented in this header; use only supported TSK_FS_JENTRY_WALK flags as defined elsewhere in TSK (unknown here).
Caller must check the returned uint8_t and handle errors/termination as defined by the TSK API (exact convention unknown here).

functions.name: ext2fs_jblk_walk
functions.signature: uint8_t ext2fs_jblk_walk(TSK_FS_INFO * a_fs, TSK_DADDR_T start_blk, TSK_DADDR_T end_blk, int flags, TSK_FS_JBLK_WALK_CB cb, void *cb_ctx);
functions.description: Iterate over raw journal blocks in an EXT* filesystem between start_blk and end_blk (inclusive or per library convention) and invoke a callback for each block. This provides lower-level access than jentry_walk by walking blocks rather than parsed entries. flags controls traversal behavior; cb is called for each visited block with cb_ctx passed through. Returns a status byte indicating success/failure or stop (exact semantics not documented here).
requirements: a_fs must be a non-NULL pointer to an initialized EXT* filesystem handle with journal access available.
cb must be non-NULL; it is invoked for each journal block visited.
start_blk and end_blk should specify a valid range within the journal address space; start_blk should not exceed end_blk (inferred from parameter names and common usage).
flags meaning and valid combinations are not documented in this header; use only supported TSK_FS_JBLK_WALK flags as defined elsewhere in TSK (unknown here).
cb_ctx may be NULL or any user-supplied context pointer.
Caller must check the returned uint8_t and handle errors/termination as defined by the TSK API (exact convention unknown here).

functions.name: ext2fs_jopen
functions.description: Open/initialize access to the filesystem journal for an EXT* filesystem. Typically used to locate and prepare the journal (JBD/JBD2), optionally using a specific journal inode (a_inum). After a successful call, journal walk functions (e.g., ext2fs_jentry_walk, ext2fs_jblk_walk) can be used. Returns a status byte indicating success or failure (exact convention not documented here).
requirements: a_fs must be a non-NULL pointer to an initialized EXT* filesystem handle.
a_inum should identify the journal inode when applicable (e.g., ext3/4 journal file); behavior for special values is not documented here (unknown).
The filesystem must support or have a journal present; otherwise the call may fail (inferred from purpose).
Caller must check the returned uint8_t and handle errors accordingly; exact success/error values are not specified here.

functions.name: fatfs_inum_is_in_range
functions.description: Checks whether the given metadata address (inode number) is within the valid range for the specified FAT file system instance. Intended as a lightweight validation helper before performing inode-based operations. Return-value semantics (true/nonzero vs. FATFS_OK/FATFS_FAIL) are not documented here; treat the return as a boolean indicator of in-range status.
requirements: a_fatfs must be a valid, initialized FATFS_INFO for an opened FAT/exFAT file system.
a_inum should be an inode number that may or may not be in range; no specific bounds are documented here.
Callers must interpret the uint8_t return as an indicator; exact values for in-range vs. out-of-range are not specified in this header.

functions.name: fatfs_ptr_arg_is_null
functions.signature: uint8_t fatfs_ptr_arg_is_null(void *ptr, const char *param_name, const char *func_name);
functions.description: Helper that indicates whether a pointer argument is NULL, with context strings for the parameter and calling function names. Useful for centralized argument validation and logging. Return-value semantics (true/nonzero vs. FATFS_OK/FATFS_FAIL) are not documented here; treat the return as a boolean indicator of nullness.
requirements: param_name should point to a null-terminated C string naming the parameter, or be NULL if not available.
func_name should point to a null-terminated C string naming the function, or be NULL if not available.
No side effects on ptr; used only for validation/reporting.
Callers must interpret the uint8_t return as an indicator; exact mapping is not specified in this header.

functions.name: fatfs_inum_arg_is_in_range
functions.signature: uint8_t fatfs_inum_arg_is_in_range(FATFS_INFO *a_fatfs, TSK_INUM_T a_inum, const char *func_name);
functions.description: Validates that an inode argument is within range for the given FATFS_INFO, optionally annotating the check with the name of the calling function. Intended for argument checking prior to inode operations. Return-value semantics are not specified; treat as a boolean indicator.
requirements: a_fatfs must be a valid, initialized FATFS_INFO.
func_name may be NULL or a null-terminated string with the caller’s name.
Callers must interpret the uint8_t return as an indicator; exact mapping is not specified in this header.

functions.name: fatfs_dos_2_unix_time
functions.signature: time_t fatfs_dos_2_unix_time(uint16_t date, uint16_t time, uint8_t timetens);
functions.description: Converts a FAT/DOS on-disk date and time (and 10ms units field) into a Unix time_t. Use when decoding directory entry timestamps.
requirements: date should encode a valid FAT date; time should encode a valid FAT time (see FATFS_ISDATE and FATFS_ISTIME macros for validity).
timetens should be the 10ms fractional time component as stored on disk; exact accepted range is not stated here.
If date/time are invalid, returned value behavior is unspecified in this header.

functions.name: fatfs_dos_2_nanosec
functions.description: Converts the FAT/DOS 10-millisecond time units field (timetens) into nanoseconds for sub-second timestamp precision.
requirements: timetens should be the raw on-disk 10ms units value; exact permitted range is not specified here.
Return is a nanosecond value corresponding to timetens; overflow/invalid value behavior is not documented.

functions.name: fatfs_utf16_inode_str_2_utf8
functions.signature: TSKConversionResult fatfs_utf16_inode_str_2_utf8(FATFS_INFO *a_fatfs, UTF16 *src, size_t src_len, UTF8 *dest, size_t dest_len, TSK_INUM_T a_inum, const char *a_desc);
functions.description: Converts a UTF-16 string (typically from an on-disk FAT/exFAT entry) into UTF-8, using file-system context and inode number for validation/diagnostics. Intended for decoding long file names or exFAT names. Returns a TSKConversionResult indicating success or specific conversion issues.
requirements: a_fatfs must be a valid FATFS_INFO.
src must point to a UTF-16 buffer of length src_len (in UTF16 code units).
dest must point to a writable buffer of size dest_len (in bytes).
dest_len must be large enough to hold the converted UTF-8 including terminator; no explicit minimum specified here. FATFS_MAXNAMLEN_UTF8 may be relevant for typical name sizes.
a_desc may be a descriptive string for logging/diagnostics; may be NULL.
Behavior for invalid encoding sequences depends on TSKConversionResult; specifics are not documented here.

functions.name: fatfs_cleanup_ascii

functions.description: Opens a directory by metadata address (inode/CNID) within the HFS filesystem and returns a populated TSK_FS_DIR via output parameter. Intended for enumerating directory entries given an inum and optional flags.

functions.name: hfs_name_cmp

Return value should be interpreted as strcmp-style ordering; exact normalization behavior is not documented here (unknown).

functions.name: hfs_jopen
functions.description: Opens the HFS+ journal associated with the given filesystem, likely using the Journal Info Block and/or special files to locate it. The TSK_INUM_T may specify a related metadata object (e.g., journal file CNID). Returns status as uint8_t.

TSK_INUM_T must be valid in the context provided (exact meaning is not specified here; unknown).

functions.signature: uint8_t hfs_jblk_walk(TSK_FS_INFO * , TSK_DADDR_T , TSK_DADDR_T , int , TSK_FS_JBLK_WALK_CB , void * );
functions.description: Iterates over blocks in the HFS+ journal between the given start and end block addresses, invoking a caller-supplied block-walk callback for each block. The int parameter supplies walk flags. Returns a status byte indicating success/failure.

Caller must check return status and handle errors; the callback may influence traversal (per TSK callback contract, not specified here).

functions.name: hfs_jentry_walk
functions.description: Walks entries (transactions/records) in the HFS+ journal, invoking a caller-provided journal entry callback for each entry. The int parameter supplies walk flags/controls. Returns a status byte indicating success/failure.
requirements: TSK_FS_INFO* must be valid and associated journal must be accessible (open).
The flags (int) must be values supported by the TSK journal entry walker (not defined here).
TSK_FS_JENTRY_WALK_CB callback must be a valid function pointer; void* is user data passed to it.
Callers must check the uint8_t return value and handle traversal errors.

functions.name: hfs_follow_hard_link
functions.signature: TSK_INUM_T hfs_follow_hard_link(HFS_INFO * hfs, hfs_file * entry, unsigned char *is_error);
functions.description: Resolves an HFS+ file that is a hard link to its target by inspecting the file’s metadata and returns the CNID (inum) of the link target. Sets is_error to indicate whether an error occurred during resolution versus a non-link case.

Callers should examine both the returned TSK_INUM_T and is_error to distinguish errors from ‘not a hard link’ cases.

functions.name: hfs_cat_file_lookup

Caller must check the returned uint8_t status and handle errors.

functions.name: error_returned

functions.name: hfs_is_hard_link

functions.name: hfs_cat_traverse

functions.description: Traverses the HFS Catalog B-tree and invokes the provided callback for records/keys. The callback receives node level/type, the current key, key length, node size, and on-disk key offset, and returns control codes (HFS_BTREE_CB_*). Returns a status byte for overall traversal.
requirements: hfs must be a valid HFS_INFO pointer with catalog file and header initialized.

a_cb must be a valid function pointer of type TSK_HFS_BTREE_CB. The callback must return one of: HFS_BTREE_CB_IDX_LT, HFS_BTREE_CB_IDX_EQGT, HFS_BTREE_CB_LEAF_GO, HFS_BTREE_CB_LEAF_STOP, or HFS_BTREE_CB_ERR, as appropriate.
ptr is an opaque user data pointer passed through to the callback; may be NULL.
Caller must check the uint8_t return code and handle traversal or callback-reported errors.

functions.name: hfs_cat_get_cat_offset
functions.signature: uint8_t hfs_cat_get_cat_offset(HFS_INFO * hfs, TSK_INUM_T inum, hfs_cat_rec_off * data);
functions.description: Finds the on-disk byte offset and key length of the catalog record for the given CNID (inum) within the HFS Catalog B-tree and returns it via the provided hfs_cat_rec_off output structure. Returns status as uint8_t.
requirements: hfs must be a valid HFS_INFO with catalog initialized.
inum must be a CNID that exists in the Catalog B-tree.
data must be a non-null pointer; on success, its fields (offset, keylen) will be set to the record’s location and key length.
Caller must check the return status byte before using the output values.

Thread-safety and reentrancy are unknown; avoid concurrent use on the same TSK_FS_INFO unless documented elsewhere.

functions.name: iso9660_name_cmp

functions.description: Compares two filenames within the context of an ISO9660 filesystem, likely applying ISO9660/Joliet/Rock Ridge comparison rules (e.g., case handling, version suffixes). Returns an int consistent with strcmp-style ordering (negative, zero, positive), but exact comparison semantics are not documented in this header.

The two const char* parameters must point to valid, null-terminated C strings.
Comparison rules (case sensitivity, version numbers, character set handling) are unspecified here; callers should not rely on a particular collation without consulting implementation.

functions.name: logicalfs_read_block
functions.signature: ssize_t logicalfs_read_block(TSK_FS_INFO *a_fs, TSK_FS_FILE *a_fs_file, TSK_DADDR_T a_offset, char *buf);
functions.description: Reads a single logical file-system block from the given file into the supplied buffer. Intended for block-aligned access within a Sleuth Kit logical file system. The block size is the logical file-system block size (LOGICAL_BLOCK_SIZE), and the offset is interpreted as a block index relative to the start of the file represented by a_fs_file. a_fs_file must be a valid, opened TSK_FS_FILE associated with a_fs.
buf must be non-null and large enough to hold one logical block (>= LOGICAL_BLOCK_SIZE bytes).
a_offset must be a valid non-negative block index within the file; reading past the end of the file may return fewer bytes or an error (behavior not explicitly documented).
