Thread-safety and reentrancy are unknown; avoid concurrent mutation of a_fs or a_fs_file from other threads while reading.

requirements: a_fs must point to a valid, initialized TSK_FS_INFO for a logical file system.
a_fs_file must be a valid, opened TSK_FS_FILE associated with a_fs.
buf must be non-null and have capacity for at least len bytes.
len may be zero (no-op) or positive; extremely large values may be constrained by implementation (not documented).
a_offset must be a valid non-negative byte offset within the file; reads that extend past EOF may return fewer bytes or zero.
Callers must check the return value: negative indicates an error; a non-negative value < len may indicate EOF or a partial read.
Thread-safety and reentrancy are unknown; avoid concurrent mutation of a_fs or a_fs_file from other threads while reading.

functions.name: nt2unixtime
functions.description: Converts an NT time (FILETIME-style 100-nanosecond intervals since 1601-01-01 UTC) into a Unix epoch time in seconds. Use to map NTFS timestamps to Unix seconds for reporting or comparison. The fractional sub-second component is discarded; combine with nt2nano() if needed.
requirements: ntdate is expected to be a Windows/NT FILETIME value (count of 100 ns ticks since 1601-01-01 UTC).
Caller should not assume any specific sentinel for invalid input; if the source timestamp is 0 or pre-epoch, the conversion may return 0 seconds (unknown exact policy without implementation).

functions.name: nt2nano
functions.description: Returns the nanosecond component derived from an NT time (FILETIME-style) for pairing with nt2unixtime(). Intended to provide the sub-second (0–999,999,999) portion corresponding to the given NT timestamp.
requirements: ntdate is expected to be a Windows/NT FILETIME value (count of 100 ns ticks since 1601-01-01 UTC).
The returned value represents only the fractional nanoseconds within the second; combine with nt2unixtime() for a full Unix timestamp.
Range of return is expected to be 0..999,999,999 (exact behavior for invalid inputs is unknown).

functions.name: ntfs_find_file
functions.signature: uint8_t ntfs_find_file(TSK_FS_INFO *fs, TSK_INUM_T inode_toid, uint32_t type_toid, uint8_t type_used, uint16_t id_toid, uint8_t id_used, TSK_FS_DIR_WALK_FLAG_ENUM dir_walk_flags, TSK_FS_DIR_WALK_CB action, void *ptr);

Caller must check the return value for success/failure.

functions.name: tsk_hdb_rollback_transaction
functions.description: Roll back a previously begun transaction, discarding changes.
requirements: Argument must be a valid, open TSK_HDB_INFO pointer.
Must be called only after a successful tsk_hdb_begin_transaction call (i.e., while a transaction is active).
Caller must check the return value for success/failure.

functions.name: tsk_hdb_close
functions.description: Close an open hash database handle and release associated resources.
requirements: Argument should be a TSK_HDB_INFO pointer previously returned by tsk_hdb_open.
After closing, the handle must not be used again.
Behavior if passed NULL is not documented; callers should avoid passing NULL (inferred).

functions.name: TskHdbInfo::~TskHdbInfo
functions.description: Destructor for the C++ wrapper object; closes the underlying C handle by calling tsk_hdb_close(m_hdbInfo).
requirements: Object should have been previously constructed normally; destructor is called automatically.
After destruction, the object and its underlying handle must not be used.

functions.name: TskHdbInfo::open
functions.description: Open a hash database and associate it with this wrapper. Returns 0 on success and 1 on error.
requirements: a_dbFile must be a valid path to the database (TSK_TCHAR string).
a_flags must be a valid TSK_HDB_OPEN_ENUM value or combination.
Caller must check the return value (0 success, 1 error).

functions.name: TskHdbInfo::lookupStr
functions.signature: int8_t TskHdbInfo::lookupStr(const char *a_hash, TSK_HDB_FLAG_ENUM a_flags, TSK_HDB_LOOKUP_FN a_action, void *a_ptr);
functions.description: Search the associated database for a text/ASCII hash value. Delegates to tsk_hdb_lookup_str. Returns -1 on error, 0 if not found, 1 if found.
requirements: This instance must have been successfully opened (m_hdbInfo != NULL).
a_hash must be a valid null-terminated string.
If TSK_HDB_FLAG_QUICK is not set, a_action should be non-NULL to receive matches; a_ptr is passed through to the callback.
Caller must handle the tri-state return value.

functions.name: TskHdbInfo::lookupRaw
functions.signature: int8_t TskHdbInfo::lookupRaw(uint8_t * a_hash, uint8_t a_len, TSK_HDB_FLAG_ENUM a_flags, TSK_HDB_LOOKUP_FN a_action, void *a_ptr);
functions.description: Search the associated database for a binary-form hash value. Delegates to tsk_hdb_lookup_raw. Returns -1 on error, 0 if not found, 1 if found.
requirements: This instance must have been successfully opened (m_hdbInfo != NULL).
a_hash must point to a valid buffer of length a_len.
If TSK_HDB_FLAG_QUICK is not set, a_action should be non-NULL to receive matches; a_ptr is passed through to the callback.
Caller must handle the tri-state return value.

functions.name: TskHdbInfo::createIndex
functions.description: Create an index for the open database by delegating to tsk_hdb_make_index. The parameter is documented here as the "Text of hash database type." Returns 1 on error.
requirements: This instance must have been successfully opened (m_hdbInfo != NULL).
a_type should be a supported index type string; supported list indicated by TSK_HDB_DBTYPE_SUPPORT_STR ("nsrl-md5, nsrl-sha1, md5sum, encase, hk").
Caller must check the return value (1 on error per comment).

functions.name: TskHdbInfo::hasIndex
functions.description: Return whether an index exists for the specified hash type. Wraps tsk_hdb_has_idx.
requirements: This instance must have been successfully opened (m_hdbInfo != NULL).
a_htype must be a valid value corresponding to TSK_HDB_HTYPE_ENUM (e.g., TSK_HDB_HTYPE_MD5_ID, etc.); it is cast internally.
Return value semantics: 1 if index exists, 0 otherwise (per wrapper comment).

functions.name: TskHdbInfo::getDbType
functions.description: Return the database type for this handle, or TSK_HDB_DBTYPE_INVALID_ID on error or if not opened.
requirements: Safe to call any time; returns TSK_HDB_DBTYPE_INVALID_ID if not opened (per inline implementation).
Caller must not assume a specific type without checking the return value.

functions.name: logical_open
functions.signature: TSK_IMG_INFO *logical_open(int a_num_img, const TSK_TCHAR * const a_images[], unsigned int a_ssize);
functions.description: Opens a logical directory image and returns a TSK_IMG_INFO handle representing it. Callers supply a count and array of TSK_TCHAR path strings (e.g., one or more input images/paths) and a sector/block size parameter. Typical usage is to obtain the returned TSK_IMG_INFO* and use it with TSK image-reading APIs; on failure, NULL is returned. Cleanup/closing is not defined in this header; based on Sleuth Kit conventions, callers would typically release the handle with the appropriate TSK image close routine (exact function unknown here). Details of how multiple paths are combined and how a_ssize is interpreted are not specified in this header.
requirements: a_images must be a valid pointer to an array with at least a_num_img elements.
Each a_images[i] (0 <= i < a_num_img) must be a valid, null-terminated TSK_TCHAR string.
a_num_img must be >= 0; if > 0, it must match the number of valid entries in a_images. (Exact minimum not stated; typical expectation is >= 1.)
Callers must check the return value for NULL to detect errors.
The encoding/type of TSK_TCHAR depends on build settings; provided strings must match the build’s TSK_TCHAR (e.g., wide vs narrow).
The meaning and valid range of a_ssize are not specified here; callers should pass a value appropriate for the environment or library defaults (unknown from this header).

functions.name: clear_inum_cache_entry
functions.description: Clears a single entry in the logical image’s inum-to-path cache, identified by index. Intended to invalidate/remove cached mapping data within an IMG_LOGICAL_INFO instance. Typically used during cache maintenance or when entries become stale.
requirements: logical_img_info must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to an initialized IMG_LOGICAL_INFO.
index must be within the bounds of the inum_cache array: 0 <= index < LOGICAL_INUM_CACHE_LEN.

If the IMG_LOGICAL_INFO caches are accessed concurrently, the caller must perform appropriate synchronization consistent with the structure’s "protected by cache_lock" comment before modifying cache entries.
No return value; callers should not assume any further state changes beyond clearing the specified cache entry.

functions.name: tsk_pool_open_sing
functions.description: Open a storage pool view from a single volume-system partition. The function detects the pool type when type is TSK_POOL_TYPE_DETECT or uses the specified type. Returns a pool handle describing block size, number of blocks, and volumes. Typical usage: obtain a TSK_VS_PART_INFO from a volume system, call this to get a TSK_POOL_INFO, use it for reads/queries, then close it with tsk_pool_close. Details of error reporting are not documented here; NULL is typically returned on failure in TSK APIs.
requirements: part must be a valid, initialized TSK_VS_PART_INFO pointer and must remain valid for the lifetime of the returned pool handle.
type may be TSK_POOL_TYPE_DETECT to auto-detect or a specific supported pool type (e.g., TSK_POOL_TYPE_APFS, TSK_POOL_TYPE_LVM).
On success, the returned pointer must be released with tsk_pool_close; do not use the handle after closing.
Do not pass NULL to part (behavior on NULL is unspecified and may crash).
Expect NULL on failure (exact error mechanism not specified in this header).

functions.name: tsk_pool_open
functions.signature: const TSK_POOL_INFO *tsk_pool_open(int num_vols, const TSK_VS_PART_INFO *const parts[], TSK_POOL_TYPE_ENUM type);
functions.description: Open a storage pool view from multiple volume-system partitions (e.g., a pool spanning multiple members). Can auto-detect pool type or use the specified type. Returns a TSK_POOL_INFO handle on success for subsequent reading/queries; close with tsk_pool_close. Error details are not documented here; NULL is typically returned on failure in TSK APIs.
requirements: num_vols must be greater than 0.
parts must point to an array with at least num_vols entries.
Each parts[i] (0 <= i < num_vols) must be a valid, initialized, non-NULL TSK_VS_PART_INFO pointer and remain valid for the lifetime of the returned handle.
type may be TSK_POOL_TYPE_DETECT or a specific supported pool type.
On success, the returned pointer must be closed with tsk_pool_close; do not use after close.
Expect NULL on failure (exact error mechanism not specified in this header).

functions.name: tsk_pool_open_img_sing
functions.signature: const TSK_POOL_INFO *tsk_pool_open_img_sing(TSK_IMG_INFO *img, TSK_OFF_T offset, TSK_POOL_TYPE_ENUM type);
functions.description: Open a storage pool view within a single image at the given byte offset. The function can auto-detect the pool type or use the specified type. Use the returned TSK_POOL_INFO for reading and querying the pool; release it with tsk_pool_close.
requirements: img must be a valid, initialized TSK_IMG_INFO pointer and must remain valid for the lifetime of the pool handle.
offset is a byte offset within img to the start of the pool container; it must be non-negative and within the image bounds.
type may be TSK_POOL_TYPE_DETECT or a specific supported type.
On success, close the returned handle with tsk_pool_close; do not use after closing.
Expect NULL on failure (exact error mechanism not specified in this header).

functions.name: tsk_pool_open_img
functions.signature: const TSK_POOL_INFO *tsk_pool_open_img(int num_imgs, TSK_IMG_INFO *const imgs[], const TSK_OFF_T offsets[], TSK_POOL_TYPE_ENUM type);
functions.description: Open a storage pool view spanning multiple images, each with a corresponding byte offset to the pool member within that image. The function can auto-detect the pool type or use the specified type. Returns a TSK_POOL_INFO handle for reading/queries; close it with tsk_pool_close.
requirements: num_imgs must be greater than 0.
imgs must point to an array with at least num_imgs entries; each imgs[i] must be a valid, initialized, non-NULL TSK_IMG_INFO pointer that remains valid for the lifetime of the returned handle.
offsets must point to an array with at least num_imgs entries; each offsets[i] is a non-negative byte offset within imgs[i] to the pool member.
type may be TSK_POOL_TYPE_DETECT or a specific supported type.
On success, close the returned handle with tsk_pool_close; do not use after closing.
Expect NULL on failure (exact error mechanism not specified in this header).

functions.name: tsk_pool_close
functions.description: Close a pool handle previously returned by a tsk_pool_open* function and free associated resources. After this call, the handle and any pointers derived from it must not be used.
requirements: The argument must be a pointer previously returned by a tsk_pool_open* function and not already closed.
Do not use the handle after calling this function (use-after-free).
Behavior when passing NULL is not specified in this header (avoid passing NULL).

functions.name: tsk_pool_read
functions.signature: ssize_t tsk_pool_read(TSK_POOL_INFO *a_fs, TSK_OFF_T a_off, char *a_buf, size_t a_len);
functions.description: Read bytes from the pool at the given byte offset into the caller-provided buffer. Returns the number of bytes read, which may be less than requested, or a negative value on error (typical TSK/posix pattern). Intended for random access reads of pooled data blocks.
requirements: a_fs must be a valid, open TSK_POOL_INFO pointer (not closed).
a_off must be a non-negative byte offset within the addressable size of the pool; out-of-range offsets will fail.
a_buf must be non-NULL and point to a writable buffer of at least a_len bytes.
a_len may be zero (in which case no data is read).
Callers must check the return value: negative indicates an error; non-negative indicates bytes read (which can be less than a_len).

functions.name: tsk_pool_unallocated_runs
functions.description: Return a list/chain of unallocated extents (runs) within the pool, as a TSK_FS_ATTR_RUN list. Useful for analyzing free space. Ownership, lifetime, and how to free the returned runs are not documented here and may follow TSK conventions.
requirements: Argument must be a valid, open TSK_POOL_INFO pointer (not closed).
Caller must not modify the pool handle while relying on the returned runs list.
Ownership and deallocation method for the returned TSK_FS_ATTR_RUN are unknown from this header; consult implementation or broader TSK docs before freeing or retaining the pointer.

functions.name: tsk_pool_type_toid
functions.description: Convert a textual pool type name (TSK_TCHAR string) to its TSK_POOL_TYPE_ENUM identifier. Use to parse user input or configuration to a type enum.
requirements: str must be a non-NULL, NUL-terminated TSK_TCHAR string.
String contents should match a supported pool type name; otherwise the function returns an enum indicating unsupported/unknown (exact mapping for unknown is not documented here).

functions.name: tsk_pool_type_toid_utf8
functions.description: Convert a UTF-8 encoded pool type name to its TSK_POOL_TYPE_ENUM identifier. Use to parse UTF-8 user input into a type enum.
requirements: str must be a non-NULL, NUL-terminated UTF-8 string.
String contents should match a supported pool type name; otherwise the function returns an enum indicating unsupported/unknown (exact mapping for unknown is not documented here).

functions.name: tsk_pool_type_print
functions.description: Print the list or usage text of supported pool types to the given FILE stream (e.g., stdout or stderr). Useful for help output or diagnostics.
requirements: hFile must be a valid, open FILE* suitable for writing.
The stream should be open and writable; behavior is undefined if hFile is NULL or not writable.

functions.name: tsk_pool_type_toname
functions.description: Return the canonical name string for the given pool type enum. Useful for logging or user display. The returned pointer is expected to refer to a static string; exact behavior for unknown enums is not documented here.
requirements: ptype should be a valid TSK_POOL_TYPE_ENUM value; behavior for invalid or unsupported values is unspecified.
Treat the returned string as read-only; do not free it.

functions.name: TSKPool::uuid
functions.description: Returns a const reference to the pool's UUID. Use to retrieve a stable identifier for the pool instance. The reference remains valid as long as the TSKPool object remains alive.
requirements: Must be called on a valid, constructed TSKPool instance (or derived class).
The returned reference becomes invalid once the TSKPool object is destroyed.

functions.name: TSKPool::block_size
functions.description: Returns the logical block size for the pool, in bytes (exact unit not explicitly documented). Intended for consumers that need to align reads or interpret block-based addresses.
requirements: Must be called on a valid, constructed TSKPool instance (or derived class).
Returned value may be 0 if not initialized by the concrete implementation; caller should handle 0 as an unknown/invalid size.

functions.name: TSKPool::dev_block_size
functions.description: Returns the device block size for the underlying storage, likely in bytes (unit not explicitly documented). Useful for low-level I/O alignment.
requirements: Must be called on a valid, constructed TSKPool instance (or derived class).
Returned value may be 0 if not initialized by the concrete implementation; caller should handle 0 appropriately.

functions.name: TSKPool::num_blocks
functions.description: Returns the total number of logical blocks in the pool. Use to bound block-based addressing.
requirements: Must be called on a valid, constructed TSKPool instance (or derived class).
Returned value may be 0 if not initialized by the concrete implementation; caller should handle 0 appropriately.

functions.name: TSKPool::first_img_offset
functions.description: Returns the byte offset of the first member image in the pool. If the pool has no members, returns 0.
requirements: Must be called on a valid, constructed TSKPool instance (or derived class).
Caller must handle the case where 0 is returned either because there are no members or because the first member is at offset 0.

functions.name: TSKPool::num_vols
functions.description: Returns the number of volumes in the pool (exact semantics not documented).
requirements: Must be called on a valid, constructed TSKPool instance (or derived class).
Returned value may be 0 if not initialized or if there are no volumes; caller should handle 0 appropriately.

functions.name: TSKPool::read
functions.signature: ssize_t TSKPool::read(uint64_t address, char *buf, size_t buf_size) const noexcept
functions.description: Pure virtual read method to read data from the pool into a caller-provided buffer. The addressing unit and semantics (bytes vs. blocks) are not documented here and depend on the concrete implementation.
requirements: Must be called on a valid concrete subclass of TSKPool that implements read.
buf must point to a writable memory region of at least buf_size bytes.
buf_size may be 0 (behavior is implementation-defined/unknown).
address must be within the readable range for the implementation (exact units and bounds are unknown here).
Caller must check the returned ssize_t for success/partial read/negative error according to the implementation’s contract (not specified in this header).

functions.name: TSKPool::unallocated_ranges
functions.description: Returns a vector of unallocated ranges within the pool. The default implementation returns an empty vector; concrete subclasses may override to provide actual ranges. Each range contains start_block and num_blocks.
requirements: Must be called on a valid, constructed TSKPool instance (or derived class).
Caller should not assume non-empty results; handle the empty vector case.
Interpretation of start_block and num_blocks is in logical blocks (implied by field names); exact block size obtained via block_size().

functions.name: TSKPool::getTSKImgInfo
functions.description: Returns the TSK_IMG_INFO* for the member image at the given index, or NULL if index is out of range.
requirements: Must be called on a valid, constructed TSKPool instance (or derived class).
index must be less than the number of member images to obtain a non-NULL pointer.
Caller must check for and handle a NULL return.
The returned TSK_IMG_INFO* is owned by the TSKPool; caller must not free it (ownership not stated here but implied by storage).

functions.name: operator|=
functions.signature: template <typename T, typename = std::enable_if_t<std::is_enum<T>::value>> inline T &operator|=(T &a, T b)
functions.description: Helper free function template that performs in-place bitwise OR on enum types, enabling flag-style enums. It casts the result of a | b back to T and stores it in a.
requirements: Template parameter T must be an enum type (enforced by enable_if).
Arguments a and b must be valid values of enum type T.
a is modified in place and a reference to it is returned.

functions.name: APFSBlock::APFSBlock
functions.description: Constructs an APFSBlock object representing a specific block number within a given APFS pool and allocates internal storage for its contents. Typically used to create a block handle that can later be read/decrypted/dumped.
requirements: pool must outlive the constructed APFSBlock instance (APFSBlock stores a reference to APFSPool).
block_num must be a valid APFS block number for the referenced pool (exact valid range unknown from this header).

functions.name: APFSBlock::decrypt
functions.signature: void APFSBlock::decrypt(const uint8_t *key, const uint8_t *key2 = nullptr) noexcept
functions.description: Decrypts the block’s internal storage using the provided key material. The second key is optional and may be used for configurations requiring two keys. Intended to be called after constructing/reading a block before interpreting its contents.
requirements: key must be a valid, non-null pointer to key material of the expected size (exact size unknown from this header).
key2 may be null; if provided, it must point to valid key material (exact size unknown).
May be called multiple times; effects and idempotency are not documented (unknown).
No exceptions are thrown (noexcept).

functions.name: APFSBlock::dump
functions.description: Outputs a human-readable representation of the block’s internal contents, primarily for debugging or inspection. Does not modify state.
requirements: No preconditions are stated; safe to call on any constructed APFSBlock.
No exceptions are thrown (noexcept).
Output destination and format are not specified (unknown).

functions.name: APFSBlock::operator==
functions.description: Compares two APFSBlock instances for equality. Two blocks are equal if they refer to the same APFSPool instance and have the same block number.
requirements: rhs may refer to any APFSBlock; comparison is well-defined even if the blocks are from different pools.
No exceptions are thrown (noexcept).

functions.name: APFSBlock::operator!=
functions.description: Inequality comparison for APFSBlock. Returns the logical negation of operator==.
requirements: rhs may refer to any APFSBlock; comparison is well-defined even if the blocks are from different pools.
No exceptions are thrown (noexcept).

functions.name: APFSBlock::block_num
functions.description: Returns the APFS block number represented by this APFSBlock.
requirements: Callable on any constructed APFSBlock.
No exceptions are thrown (noexcept).

functions.name: APFSBlock::pool
functions.description: Returns a reference to the APFSPool that this block belongs to.
requirements: The returned reference remains valid only as long as the referenced APFSPool outlives the APFSBlock.
No exceptions are thrown (noexcept).

functions.name: APFSBlock::data
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the block’s internal storage buffer. Useful for reading the raw bytes of the block.
requirements: The returned pointer becomes invalid when the APFSBlock is destroyed.
The buffer must be treated as read-only; do not modify through the returned pointer.
No exceptions are thrown (noexcept).

functions.name: APFSPool::APFSPool
functions.description: Constructs an APFSPool over one or more underlying images and designates an APFS container superblock (NX) block to use (defaulting to the last known good). Sets up internal state and may prepare for volume discovery and block access.
requirements: imgs is moved into the pool; callers must not use imgs after passing it to the constructor.
Each img_t in imgs must be a valid image descriptor usable by TSK (exact requirements unknown from this header).
nx_block_num should be a valid APFS NX block number for the container (exact valid range unknown).
The constructed APFSPool is non-copyable but movable; ensure lifetimes accordingly.

functions.name: APFSPool::volumes
functions.description: Enumerates and returns the APFS volumes (file systems) contained in this pool.
requirements: Callable on a validly constructed APFSPool.
Returned vector contains APFSFileSystem objects by value; lifetimes are independent of the pool.

functions.name: APFSPool::read
functions.signature: ssize_t APFSPool::read(uint64_t address, char *buf, size_t buf_size) const noexcept final
functions.description: Reads data from the pool at the given byte address into the provided buffer. Returns the number of bytes read or a negative value on error, per TSK_IMG_INFO/TSKPool conventions.
requirements: buf must be a valid, non-null pointer to a writable memory region of at least buf_size bytes.
buf_size may be zero (results in zero bytes read); positive sizes read up to the available data.
address must refer to a valid readable byte offset within the pool (exact bounds unknown from this header).
Caller must check the return value for errors (negative values indicate failure).
No exceptions are thrown (noexcept).

functions.name: APFSPool::known_versions
functions.description: Returns a list of known NX (container superblock) versions/locations observed in the pool, each with its block number and transaction ID (xid). Useful for selecting a historical container state.
requirements: Callable on a validly constructed APFSPool.
Returned vector is by value (const-qualified temporary); caller should copy/move as needed.

functions.name: APFSPool::unallocated_ranges
functions.description: Returns a list of unallocated ranges in the pool’s address space. Each range describes a span of bytes/blocks that are not currently allocated. Useful for carving or allocation analysis.
requirements: Callable on a validly constructed APFSPool.
Returned vector is by value (const-qualified temporary); caller should copy/move as needed.
Exact semantics and units of range members are not specified in this header (unknown).

functions.name: APFSPool::nx
functions.description: Retrieves the APFS container superblock (NX) as a parsed object. Optionally validates the structure when validate is true. Returns a unique_ptr owning the resulting APFSSuperblock.
requirements: Callable on a validly constructed APFSPool.
If validate is true, callers should be prepared for a null return or internal validation handling on failure (exact error signaling unknown).
Caller assumes ownership of the returned APFSSuperblock via unique_ptr.

functions.name: APFSPool::hardware_crypto
functions.description: Indicates whether hardware-backed cryptography is available/used by this APFS pool.
requirements: Callable on a validly constructed APFSPool.
No exceptions are thrown (noexcept).

functions.name: APFSPool::clear_cache
functions.description: Clears the internal APFS block cache maintained by the pool to reclaim memory or force reloading of blocks.
requirements: Callable on a validly constructed APFSPool.
Not thread-safe per class comment; external synchronization may be required in multi-threaded use.
No exceptions are thrown (noexcept).

functions.name: LVMPool::LVMPool
functions.description: Constructs an LVMPool from a set of images, taking ownership of the provided image vector. Intended to initialize an LVM-backed TSKPool using the supplied images. This constructor is only available when compiled with HAVE_LIBVSLVM enabled.
requirements: Argument imgs must be an rvalue (e.g., passed with std::move) so that its contents can be moved into the LVMPool.
After construction, the moved-from imgs must not be used except for operations permitted on moved-from std::vector (state is valid but unspecified).
The elements of imgs must represent valid image descriptors appropriate for LVMPool/TSKPool initialization; exact structure and validity rules for img_t are unknown from this header.
Availability: This class (and thus the constructor) is compiled only when HAVE_LIBVSLVM is defined.

functions.name: LVMPool::LVMPool
functions.description: Move constructor. Transfers ownership of the underlying image/pool/LVM resources from another LVMPool into this instance. Leaves the source object in a valid but unspecified state. Useful for efficient transfers without copying underlying handles. Available only when compiled with HAVE_LIBVSLVM.
requirements: The source LVMPool object becomes moved-from; only destruction or reassignment should be performed on it thereafter (valid but unspecified state).
No exceptions are specified; behavior follows the defaulted move construction rules of the members.
Availability: This class (and thus the move constructor) is compiled only when HAVE_LIBVSLVM is defined.

functions.name: LVMPool::operator=
functions.description: Move assignment operator. Releases any current resources and takes ownership of the resources from the right-hand LVMPool, leaving it in a valid but unspecified state. Enables efficient reassignment without copying. Available only when compiled with HAVE_LIBVSLVM.
requirements: Right-hand operand becomes moved-from; only destruction or reassignment should be performed on it thereafter (valid but unspecified state).
Self-move-assignment is well-formed but generally discouraged; semantics follow the compiler-generated default move assignment of members.
The resulting object should not be used concurrently during the move operation.
Availability: This class (and thus the move assignment operator) is compiled only when HAVE_LIBVSLVM is defined.

functions.name: LVMPool::~LVMPool
functions.description: Destructor. Cleans up any resources associated with the LVMPool, such as LVM handles, file I/O pools, and image references. Invoked automatically when an LVMPool object goes out of scope or is deleted. Available only when compiled with HAVE_LIBVSLVM.
requirements: Do not use the LVMPool instance after destruction.
Ensure no concurrent operations are in progress on this LVMPool when it is destroyed (standard object lifetime requirement).
Availability: This class (and thus the destructor) is compiled only when HAVE_LIBVSLVM is defined.

functions.name: LVMPool::read
functions.signature: ssize_t LVMPool::read(uint64_t address, char *buf, size_t buf_size) const noexcept final
functions.description: Reads up to buf_size bytes from the pool at the given byte address into the provided buffer. Returns the number of bytes read on success, or a negative value on error. This overrides TSKPool::read and is marked noexcept and final.
requirements: buf must point to a writable memory region of at least buf_size bytes.
If buf_size is 0, the function performs no read and may return 0 (common convention; exact behavior not specified here).
address specifies a byte offset within the pool; reads beyond the end of the pool will fail or be truncated (exact behavior not specified here).
Caller must check the return value: a non-negative value indicates the number of bytes read; a negative value indicates an error (inferred from use of ssize_t).
Function does not throw exceptions (noexcept).
May only be called on a properly constructed LVMPool instance whose underlying resources are still valid.

functions.name: TSKPoolCompat::pool_info
functions.description: Returns a const reference to the internal TSK_POOL_INFO structure maintained by TSKPoolCompat. Intended for exposing the C-compatible pool information to C APIs or callers that need to inspect pool metadata without modifying it. The returned reference remains valid only for the lifetime of the TSKPoolCompat instance.
requirements: Caller must not attempt to modify the returned TSK_POOL_INFO (it is a const reference).
The returned reference becomes invalid once the TSKPoolCompat object is destroyed; do not store or use it after object destruction.
Thread-safety and concurrent access guarantees are unknown.

functions.name: TSKPoolCompat::~TSKPoolCompat
functions.description: Destructor for TSKPoolCompat. Cleans up the C-layer volume list (_info.vol_list) and each volume description string if they were set, ensuring the C compatibility state is released. This is called automatically when deleting a derived pool object or indirectly via the C API close callback stored in _info.close.
requirements: Do not use the object or any references (including pool_info()) after the destructor runs.
If the object was handed to C code that will call the _info.close callback, do not also delete it directly (avoid double deletion).
Derived implementations that populate _info.vol_list must ensure that volume list memory and each desc were allocated in a manner compatible with operator delete[] as used by the destructor.

functions.name: TSKPoolCompat::poolstat

functions.name: detectVolumeEncryption
functions.description: Analyzes a volume at the given disk address within a TSK image to determine whether it appears to be encrypted. The result indicates the detection method (none, signature-based, or entropy-based) and provides a short description. Typical usage: pass a valid, opened TSK_IMG_INFO and the starting offset of a volume/partition to obtain an encryption detection assessment. Ownership/lifetime of the returned encryption_detected_result is not documented in this header; caller responsibilities for freeing are unknown.
requirements: img_info must be a valid, initialized TSK_IMG_INFO obtained from The Sleuth Kit image open routines (e.g., tsk_img_open or equivalent).

offset should refer to a valid disk address within img_info; it must not point beyond the image bounds. Exact units (sectors vs bytes) are not documented here; TSK_DADDR_T typically represents a disk/sector address.
Caller should check the return value for NULL to handle failures or undetermined results.
Thread-safety and reentrancy are not documented; avoid concurrent use on the same TSK_IMG_INFO unless guaranteed by the broader TSK API.
Memory ownership of the returned pointer is not specified in this header; caller must consult implementation/docs to determine whether and how to free it.

functions.name: detectDiskEncryption

Ownership/lifetime of the returned encryption_detected_result is not documented in this header; caller responsibilities for freeing are unknown.
requirements: img_info must be a valid, initialized TSK_IMG_INFO opened via TSK APIs.
offset must be a valid disk address within the bounds of img_info; out-of-range offsets are invalid. The precise unit of TSK_DADDR_T is not specified here.

No guarantees about thread-safety are provided; synchronize external access if needed.

import random
import string
from typing import List

# Target data type: printf-format string
# Fuzzer stubs fetch FUZZ_PARAM_STR() many times to be used as %s arguments or printed.
# We should return a bytes buffer that, when split by the harness, yields interesting
# valid strings. We'll construct multiple NUL-terminated segments with varied content
# (plain ASCII, UTF-8, long/short, with percent signs escaped or literal, edge chars).

def _rand_ascii(r: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> str:
    length = r.randint(min_len, max_len)
    alphabet = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + " _-.:,/+@#[]{}()"
    return ''.join(r.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(length))

def _rand_utf8(r: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> str:
    # Mix ASCII and some UTF-8 sequences
    length = r.randint(min_len, max_len)
    out: List[str] = []
    for _ in range(length):
        t = r.random()
        if t < 0.75:
            out.append(r.choice(string.ascii_letters + string.digits + " _-"))
        elif t < 0.88:
            # 2-byte UTF-8
            cp = r.randint(0x00A1, 0x07FF)
            out.append(chr(cp))
        elif t < 0.97:
            # 3-byte UTF-8 (BMP excluding surrogates)
            cp = r.randint(0x0800, 0xD7FF)
            out.append(chr(cp))
        else:
            # Emoji range (plane 1)
            cp = r.randint(0x1F300, 0x1FAFF)
            try:
                out.append(chr(cp))
            except ValueError:
                pass
    return ''.join(out)

def _with_percent_sequences(r: random.Random, base: str) -> str:
    # Insert benign printf-like sequences that are safe when used as plain strings
    # because they are not used as format strings in the stubs; only content printed with %s.
    inserts = ["100%", "%", "%%", "% done", "%user", "%20", "%-5", "%#x", "%zu", "%s"]
    parts = [base]
    for _ in range(r.randint(1, 3)):
        idx = r.randint(0, len(parts[-1])) if parts[-1] else 0
        ins = r.choice(inserts)
        cur = parts[-1]
        parts[-1] = cur[:idx] + ins + cur[idx:]
    return parts[-1]

def _edge_cases() -> List[str]:
    return [
        "",  # empty string
        "a",  # single char
        "0" * 64,
        "A" * 255,
        "\n",  # newline
        "\t",  # tab
        " % ",
        "%%%%%%",  # many percent signs
        "end-with-null?",  # typical
        "path/like/thing.txt",
        "key=value&x=1&y=2",
    ]

def _build_segments(r: random.Random) -> List[bytes]:
    segs: List[bytes] = []

    # Include deterministic edge cases
    for s in _edge_cases():
        segs.append(s.encode('utf-8') + b"\x00")

    # Random ASCII and UTF-8 strings
    for _ in range(r.randint(5, 10)):
        s = _rand_ascii(r, 5, 60)
        if r.random() < 0.5:
            s = _with_percent_sequences(r, s)
        segs.append(s.encode('utf-8') + b"\x00")

    for _ in range(r.randint(5, 10)):
        s = _rand_utf8(r, 4, 40)
        if r.random() < 0.4:
            s = _with_percent_sequences(r, s)
        segs.append(s.encode('utf-8', errors='ignore') + b"\x00")

    # Very long string but within limit
    long_s = _rand_ascii(r, 300, 600)
    segs.append(long_s.encode('utf-8') + b"\x00")

    # Strings containing printf-like tokens safely (since used as %s)
    tokens = [
        "value=%d; hex=%#x; str=%s; size=%zu",
        "{\"json\": true, \"num\": %u, \"msg\": \"ok\"}",
        "%% literal percent and number %llu in text",
    ]
    for t in tokens:
        segs.append(t.encode('utf-8') + b"\x00")

    return segs


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)

    # Build a buffer composed of multiple NUL-terminated strings so that
    # FUZZ_PARAM_STR() can pick different slices. Keep under 4096 bytes.
    segs = _build_segments(r)

    # Randomize order for variation with the same seed pattern
    r.shuffle(segs)

    out = bytearray()
    for seg in segs:
        if len(out) + len(seg) > 4096:
            break
        out += seg

    # Ensure buffer ends with a NUL to avoid reading past end
    if not out or out[-1] != 0:
        out += b"\x00"

    return bytes(out)

import os
import random
import struct
import string
from typing import List

# Target: generate valid initial buffers for a "filesystem path string"
# The harness calls FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME() to obtain a path to existing data
# in the sandbox. We therefore emit bytes that describe a small valid disk-image-
# like file set in a directory layout the fuzzer will mirror. Since we cannot
# perform I/O here, we generate textual content that the fuzzer runtime will map
# into files. Common practice is to emit a manifest-like buffer containing one
# or more path entries with separators. Many fuzzing harnesses that support
# FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME interpret the provided bytes as file contents for a single
# file, then expose its filename; others materialize multiple files from a
# tar-like encoding. To maximize usefulness while staying generic, we generate
# a single plausible raw image payload so any provided filename will point to
# valid data for tsk_img_open* autodetection or raw mode.
#
# Strategy:
# - Build a small RAW disk-like buffer with recognizable structures at LBA 0:
#   * Minimal DOS/MBR sector with 0x55AA signature and a simple partition table
#     (single partition spanning the disk). Many TSK open paths can handle RAW
#     with or without valid MBR; including it improves autodetection.
# - Keep size modest (<4096 bytes) as requested.
# - The buffer will be the content backing the returned filename when the fuzzer
#   maps it, so the filename string itself can be any path; the harness supplies it.
# - Randomize within valid ranges using the seed while preserving validity.
#
# Note: We return bytes, not a path string. FUZZER infra will place these bytes
# into a file and FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME will return its path.

SECTOR_SIZE = 512


def _le32(x: int) -> bytes:
    return struct.pack('<I', x & 0xFFFFFFFF)


def _le16(x: int) -> bytes:
    return struct.pack('<H', x & 0xFFFF)


def _build_mbr(total_sectors: int, start_lba: int = 2048) -> bytes:
    # Construct a minimal DOS MBR sector with one partition entry.
    # CHS fields are largely ignored by modern parsers; we set them to plausible values.
    boot = bytearray(SECTOR_SIZE)
    # x86 jump + OEM (not strictly required for parsing, but nice to have)
    boot[0:3] = b"\xEB\x3C\x90"  # JMP short + NOP
    boot[3:11] = b"TSKRAW  "      # OEM name (8 bytes)

    # Partition table at offset 446 (0x1BE), 4 entries of 16 bytes each
    ptoff = 446
    entry = bytearray(16)
    # Bootable flag 0x80 optional; set non-bootable 0x00
    entry[0] = 0x00
    # CHS start
    entry[1:4] = b"\x01\x01\x00"  # head 1, sector 1, cylinder 0
    # Partition type: 0x07 (NTFS/exFAT), common enough for tools
    entry[4] = 0x07
    # CHS end (dummy large values)
    entry[5:8] = b"\xFE\xFF\xFF"
    # LBA start
    entry[8:12] = _le32(start_lba)
    # Number of sectors
    part_secs = max(1, total_sectors - start_lba)
    entry[12:16] = _le32(part_secs)
    boot[ptoff:ptoff+16] = entry

    # MBR signature 0x55AA
    boot[510:512] = b"\x55\xAA"
    return bytes(boot)


def _pad_to(x: bytes, size: int) -> bytes:
    if len(x) >= size:
        return x[:size]
    return x + b"\x00" * (size - len(x))


def _mk_random(seed: int) -> random.Random:
    rng = random.Random()
    rng.seed(seed)
    return rng


def _build_raw_image(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Choose total size between 1 and 8 sectors (512..4096 bytes)
    sectors = rng.randint(2, 8)
    total_bytes = sectors * SECTOR_SIZE

    # Place an MBR at LBA 0
    start_lba = 1 if sectors <= 2 else rng.choice([1, 2, 2048 if sectors * SECTOR_SIZE >= 2048*SECTOR_SIZE else 1])
    # If start_lba would exceed size, clamp to 1
    if start_lba >= sectors:
        start_lba = 1
    mbr = _build_mbr(sectors, start_lba)

    # Fill remaining sectors with patterned data to resemble a volume boot sector
    body = bytearray(total_bytes - SECTOR_SIZE)
    # Simple pattern and a secondary signature in the first sector of the partition
    if len(body) >= SECTOR_SIZE and start_lba == 1:
        vbr = bytearray(SECTOR_SIZE)
        vbr[0:3] = b"\xEB\x58\x90"
        vbr[3:11] = b"MSDOS5.0"
        # bytes/sector 512
        vbr[11:13] = _le16(SECTOR_SIZE)
        # sectors per cluster = 1
        vbr[13] = 0x01
        # reserved sectors
        vbr[14:16] = _le16(1)
        # number of FATs
        vbr[16] = 0x02
        # media descriptor
        vbr[21] = 0xF8
        # hidden sectors
        vbr[28:32] = _le32(0)
        # total sectors 32-bit
        vbr[32:36] = _le32(max(1, len(body)//SECTOR_SIZE))
        # Signature
        vbr[510:512] = b"\x55\xAA"
        body[0:SECTOR_SIZE] = vbr
    # Random noise for the rest but deterministic
    for i in range(SECTOR_SIZE, len(body)):
        body[i] = rng.randrange(0, 256)

    return mbr + bytes(body)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    """
    Produce a small, valid raw disk-like image buffer suitable for FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME()
    consumers such as tsk_img_open* and logical_open. The buffer is <= 4096 bytes and
    contains a valid MBR signature and a plausible VBR-like sector to aid autodetection.
    """
    rng = _mk_random(seed)
    img = _build_raw_image(rng)
    # Ensure size limit
    if len(img) > 4096:
        img = img[:4096]
    return img

import random
import struct
from typing import List

# We generate arbitrary binary blobs intended to be fed to FUZZ_PARAM_STR in
# stubs exercising MD5/SHA-1, zlib_inflate sources, and FAT/exFAT dentry parsers.
# Strategy:
# - Produce buffers that are valid and interesting across consumers:
#   * Mixture of sizes: small, exact block multiples (64 for MD5), and larger up to a cap.
#   * Include repeating patterns, ASCII text, binary noise, and structured 32-byte segments
#     resembling FAT/exFAT directory entries (so that exfat parsers get enough bytes).
#   * Occasionally include valid small zlib streams (to help zlib_inflate succeed).
# - Keep total output <= 4096 bytes.

# Minimal DEFLATE (zlib) streams for common payloads
# Precomputed valid zlib streams (RFC1950) for small literals.
_ZLIB_SAMPLES = [
    # "": empty (deflate of empty) => 0x78 0x9c 0x03 0x00 0x00 0x00 0x00 0x01
    bytes([0x78, 0x9C, 0x03, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x01]),
    # "hello" (zlib compressed)
    bytes([0x78, 0x9C, 0xCB, 0x48, 0xCD, 0xC9, 0xC9, 0x07, 0x00, 0x06, 0x2C, 0x02, 0x15]),
    # 100 'A's
    bytes([0x78,0x9C,0x4B,0x4C,0x4A,0x06,0x00,0x08,0xC4,0x02,0x59]),
]

# Build a plausible FAT/exFAT 32-byte directory entry (primary FILE dir entry baseline)
def make_fat_dentry(rng: random.Random, name8: str = "FILE", ext3: str = "TXT", size: int = None) -> bytes:
    name = (name8.upper() + "        ")[:8].encode("ascii", "ignore")
    ext = (ext3.upper() + "   ")[:3].encode("ascii", "ignore")
    attrib = 0x20  # archive
    ntbyte = 0
    ctimeten = 0
    def dos_time():
        # pack rudimentary valid DOS time/date (little endian)
        hh = rng.randrange(0, 24)
        mm = rng.randrange(0, 60)
        ss2 = rng.randrange(0, 30)  # seconds/2
        time = (hh << 11) | (mm << 5) | ss2
        yyyy = rng.randrange(2000, 2030)
        mm2 = rng.randrange(1, 12)
        dd = rng.randrange(1, 28)
        date = ((yyyy - 1980) << 9) | (mm2 << 5) | dd
        return struct.pack('<H', time), struct.pack('<H', date)
    ctime, cdate = dos_time()
    adate = cdate
    wtime, wdate = dos_time()
    highclust = struct.pack('<H', rng.randrange(0, 0xFFFF))
    startclust = struct.pack('<H', rng.randrange(0, 0xFFFF))
    if size is None:
        size = rng.randrange(0, 1 << 20)
    size_b = struct.pack('<I', size)
    parts = [name, ext, bytes([attrib, ntbyte, ctimeten]), ctime, cdate, adate,
             highclust, wtime, wdate, startclust, size_b]
    return b"".join(parts)

# Build a 32-byte exFAT FILE primary dir entry header-like blob
# Not strictly validated, but shaped to expected fields to guide parsers
def make_exfat_file_primary(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    b = bytearray(32)
    b[0] = 0x85  # allocated FILE entry (0x85)
    b[1] = rng.randrange(2, 19)  # secondary count
    # checksum (2)
    # attrs (2)
    attrs = 0x0020  # archive
    b[4:6] = struct.pack('<H', attrs)
    # timestamps
    for off in (8, 10, 12, 14, 16, 18):
        b[off:off+2] = struct.pack('<H', rng.randrange(0, 0xFFFF))
    # tenths + tz
    b[20] = 0
    b[21] = 0
    b[22] = 0
    b[23] = 0
    b[24] = 0
    # rest reserved
    return bytes(b)

# Build an exFAT stream extension (32 bytes)
def make_exfat_stream(rng: random.Random, name_len: int, data_len: int) -> bytes:
    b = bytearray(32)
    b[0] = 0xC0  # allocated stream entry
    b[1] = 0  # flags
    b[3] = max(0, min(255, name_len))
    # file name hash
    b[4:6] = struct.pack('<H', rng.randrange(0, 0xFFFF))
    # valid data length
    b[8:16] = struct.pack('<Q', data_len)
    # first cluster (kept small)
    b[20:24] = struct.pack('<I', rng.randrange(2, 1000))
    # data length
    b[24:32] = struct.pack('<Q', data_len)
    return bytes(b)

# Build an exFAT file name entry (32 bytes), up to 15 UTF-16 chars
def make_exfat_name(rng: random.Random, name: str) -> bytes:
    b = bytearray(32)
    b[0] = 0xC1  # allocated file name entry
    b[1] = 0
    # UTF-16LE name segment (max 15 code units -> 30 bytes)
    enc = name.encode('utf-16le', 'ignore')[:30]
    b[2:2+len(enc)] = enc
    return bytes(b)

# Concatenate a few 32-byte entries to form a plausible directory sector
def make_dir_sector(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    out = bytearray()
    # exFAT set: FILE primary + STREAM + 1-3 NAME entries
    filename = "Test_%d" % rng.randrange(0, 1000)
    data_len = rng.randrange(0, 4096)
    out += make_exfat_file_primary(rng)
    out += make_exfat_stream(rng, len(filename), data_len)
    n_name = rng.randrange(1, 4)
    for i in range(n_name):
        seg = filename[i*15:(i+1)*15]
        out += make_exfat_name(rng, seg)
    # Pad to a multiple of 32 bytes
    while len(out) % 32 != 0:
        out += bytes(1)
    # Also append a standard FAT dentry for variety
    out += make_fat_dentry(rng)
    return bytes(out)

# Construct blocks targeting MD5/SHA block boundaries
def make_hash_blocks(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # MD5 block size is 64. We create sequences of exact multiples and near multiples.
    pieces: List[bytes] = []
    # 64 bytes of 'A'
    pieces.append(b"A" * 64)
    # 63 bytes of 'B' then 1 byte of NUL
    pieces.append(b"B" * 63 + b"\x00")
    # 128 bytes pseudo-random
    pr = bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(128))
    pieces.append(pr)
    return b"".join(pieces)

# Optionally return a valid small zlib stream or plain bytes
def maybe_zlib(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        return rng.choice(_ZLIB_SAMPLES)
    # produce deflate-friendly content (repeating pattern)
    token = ("PATTERN_%d" % rng.randrange(0, 100)).encode()
    return token * rng.randrange(5, 50)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    chunks: List[bytes] = []

    # 1) Directory sector-like data to feed FAT/exFAT parsers and generic consumers
    if rng.random() < 0.8:
        chunks.append(make_dir_sector(rng))

    # 2) Hash-friendly blocks to exercise MD5/SHA updates (multiple Update calls)
    if rng.random() < 0.9:
        chunks.append(make_hash_blocks(rng))

    # 3) A zlib-valid or compressible segment for zlib_inflate src
    chunks.append(maybe_zlib(rng))

    # 4) ASCII text with mixed binary to simulate file contents
    ascii_base = (
        b"The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog.\n"
        b"SleuthKit fuzz seed: %d\n" % (seed % 1000000)
    )
    noise = bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(rng.randrange(16, 64)))
    chunks.append(ascii_base + noise)

    # 5) Ensure we have at least 32 bytes (needed by several stubs)
    if sum(len(c) for c in chunks) < 32:
        chunks.append(bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(32)))

    # Interleave with some repeating patterns and NULs to vary content
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        chunks.append(b"\x00" * rng.randrange(8, 64))
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        p = bytes([rng.randrange(0, 256)])
        chunks.append(p * rng.randrange(16, 128))

    # Assemble and cap to 4096 bytes
    out = b"".join(chunks)
    if len(out) > 4096:
        out = out[:4096]

    return out
